NetApp Inc. (ISIN US64120B1098) stock is trading near its recent highs after the data storage specialist reported record fiscal first quarter 2027 results, with revenue rising 30.0 percent year over year to USD 2.02 billion and adjusted EPS jumping 66.0 percent to USD 2.58 as of Q1 fiscal 2027, according to Zacks on September 8, 2026.
Strong Q1 figures and higher fiscal 2027 guidance
NetApp delivered what it described as record results for its fiscal first quarter 2027, with Q1 revenue of USD 2.02 billion compared with market expectations of around USD 1.84 billion, beating consensus by nearly 10 percent as reported by Zacks on September 8, 2026.
On the bottom line, NetApp's adjusted EPS for Q1 fiscal 2027 reached USD 2.58, up 66 percent from the prior-year quarter and well ahead of analyst expectations of USD 2.13, marking a roughly 21 percent outperformance versus consensus according to Zacks on September 8, 2026.
Reflecting this momentum, management significantly raised its fiscal 2027 guidance, now expecting revenue between USD 7.98 billion and USD 8.23 billion and adjusted EPS in a range of USD 9.73 to USD 10.03, up from earlier targets as noted by Zacks on September 8, 2026.
AI and cloud demand support the story, but risks remain
Beyond the headline numbers, NetApp emphasized AI and cloud infrastructure trends as key drivers of its outlook at recent industry conferences. At the Goldman Sachs Communacopia plus Technology Conference 2026, the company described a strong start to fiscal 2027 and highlighted that AI workloads and cloud storage demand are lifting its pipeline, according to Investing.com on September 8, 2026.
At Citi's 2026 Global TMT Conference on September 8, 2026, NetApp reiterated that demand remained strong across its business, supported by AI adoption and infrastructure modernization, while repeating that fiscal first quarter 2027 revenue exceeded guidance across the board, as reported by Investing.com on September 8, 2026.
Management also acknowledged headwinds such as higher component costs, supply tightness and intense competition in storage and data management, suggesting that maintaining margins will require careful pricing and product differentiation, according to Investing.com on September 8, 2026.
Analyst view and valuation metrics around the consensus target
The strong quarter and raised guidance have reinforced positive analyst sentiment, but valuation is becoming a discussion point. NetApp currently carries a consensus rating of Hold across 16 analysts, with 6 Buy ratings and 10 Hold ratings and an average price target of USD 192.07, according to MarketBeat on September 8, 2026.
The same overview from MarketBeat on September 8, 2026 shows a high price target of USD 219.00 and a low target of USD 150.00 for NetApp, implying potential upside of about 1.6 percent from the average target versus the latest trading levels.
Zacks highlighted NetApp as one of its Investment Ideas on September 8, 2026, noting that both NetApp and networking firm Ciena crushed quarterly earnings expectations and raised their outlooks, and assigning NetApp a Zacks Rank number 2 (Buy) based on favorable earnings estimate revisions, according to Zacks on September 8, 2026.
At the same time, a detailed post-earnings analysis from Charged Alpha's Stock Encyclopedia argued that NetApp's 29.9 percent reported revenue growth in Q1 fiscal 2027 relies partly on a 53-week fiscal year and pricing effects, estimating underlying growth closer to 20.6 percent when adjusted for the extra week, and noting that free cash flow fell 35 percent to USD 401 million even as net income rose 61 percent, according to Charged Alpha Stock Encyclopedia on September 9, 2026.
For income-oriented investors, NetApp continues to offer a modest dividend yield. Recent institutional filings compiled by MarketBeat on September 9, 2026 note that NetApp declared a quarterly dividend of USD 0.52 per share, corresponding to an annualized payout of USD 2.08 and a yield around 1.1 percent based on recent prices, with a payout ratio of roughly 29.34 percent.
The same set of filings shows active trading in the shareholder base, with California State Teachers Retirement System reported as buying NetApp shares and asset manager Amundi reported as selling holdings, according to separate institutional alerts from MarketBeat and MarketBeat both dated September 9, 2026, underlining that large investors are actively repositioning around the stock after the strong quarter.
Another filing summary from MarketBeat on September 9, 2026 reports that Empirical Finance LLC acquired 5,617 NetApp shares, further illustrating institutional appetite following the latest earnings release and guidance update.
Stock performance and valuation as of early September 2026
As of September 8, 2026, NetApp shares traded in a daily range between USD 182.53 and USD 190.21 on Nasdaq, with a market capitalization of around USD 37.15 billion and a trailing price-earnings ratio of approximately 26.68, according to price data from MarketBeat updated on September 8, 2026.
The same overview lists a 52-week trading range for NetApp between USD 93.69 and USD 209.06, meaning that the early September 2026 price in the high USD 180s sits well above the midpoint of that band but still below the 52-week high, as shown by MarketBeat on September 8, 2026.
Zacks noted on September 9, 2026 that NetApp shares had gained 14.8 percent over the prior three months, supported by growth in all-flash arrays, AI-related deal activity and earnings momentum, and assigned the stock a Momentum Score of A, indicating favorable technical and earnings-trend characteristics, according to Zacks.
Against the backdrop of record Q1 fiscal 2027 results, a raised full-year outlook and a share price in the high USD 180s as of September 8, 2026 on Nasdaq, NetApp stock now trades close to the consensus price target of USD 192.07, leaving investors to weigh continued AI and cloud-driven growth against valuation, margin and supply-chain risks in the coming quarters.

NetApp Unveils Novus, AI Data Engine Upgrades to Power Agentic AI
Interested in NetApp, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.
NetApp unveiled Novus, a disaggregated storage architecture designed for large AI factories and GPU clusters exceeding 100,000 GPUs, with claimed performance of up to 100 TB per second and a zettabyte-scale file system.
The company expanded its AI Data Engine to discover and activate heterogeneous enterprise data across storage systems and clouds without requiring migration. NetApp will offer the platform and new metadata capabilities free for the first six months.
NetApp also introduced broader hybrid-cloud management, security and recovery tools, while expanding partnerships with Oracle Cloud, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure to support enterprise and sovereign AI workloads.
5 Tech Stocks Holding Their Ground Through the AI Trade Pullback
NetApp (NASDAQ:NTAP) used its INSIGHT 2026 event to outline a strategy for helping enterprises prepare data infrastructure for agentic AI, announcing expanded cloud partnerships, enhancements to its AI Data Engine and management platform, and a new high-scale storage architecture called NetApp Novus.
George Kurian said organizations seeking to move AI projects from pilot programs into production face two core issues: infrastructure constraints and difficulty harnessing fragmented enterprise data. He said AI systems require increasingly large GPU clusters and datasets, while unstructured information remains dispersed across storage systems, clouds, remote offices and sovereignty jurisdictions.
→ Advanced Micro Devices Is Spending $8.2 Billion to Learn What AI Needs Next
Is Backblaze the Next Momentum Monster?
"Data is becoming the constraint to productively scale AI," Kurian said. He cited NetApp's view that 93% of organizations report at least one data challenge blocking their AI ambitions.
AI Data Engine expands beyond NetApp data
Syam Nair, NetApp's Chief Product Officer, said the company's platform is intended to provide AI-ready data, proactive protection, unified storage and complete control across hybrid environments. He said the goal is to activate data where it resides rather than require customers to copy or migrate it.
→ JPMorgan Bets on Genius Sports as the Market Loses Patience
Semtech Stock Climbs as AI Boom Drives Turnaround Success
Nair announced that the metadata capability of the NetApp AI Data Engine will support heterogeneous data sources, extending beyond NetApp-managed data. The software-defined capability is designed to discover, understand and activate data across an enterprise estate without moving it into another system, according to Nair.
NetApp said it will make the AI Data Engine and its new metadata capability available free for the first six months. Nair said the platform is intended to surface data patterns and context while applying governance and protection policies.
→ AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird Progress Comes With Several Risks Still Unresolved
The company also highlighted its acquisition of DataPelago. Nair said DataPelago is designed to accelerate existing tools used by researchers and data teams, including Spark, Trino and Python libraries, within the data infrastructure and without code changes.
Security, recovery and hybrid management
Nair said NetApp is pursuing what it calls "zero trust data security," with protection built into data rather than centered solely on network posture or identity checks. He said AI readiness and data protection must operate together because autonomous agents could act on compromised information at machine speed.
NetApp also described expanded integration with Commvault. According to Nair, potential ransomware attacks will be surfaced within the Commvault interface, while NetApp's SnapRestore and curated clean recovery capabilities will support recovery workflows.
For hybrid infrastructure management, the company introduced the NetApp Console, which Nair described as a control plane for on-premises systems, Keystone and major public clouds. The console includes AI-assisted operations intended to predict issues, resolve incidents and optimize capacity and costs with human oversight.
NetApp said the console can also operate in local, air-gapped environments. Nair said existing Active IQ Unified Manager customers will have an upgrade path rather than need to replace their management tooling.
The company additionally unveiled Keystone Sovereign, an add-on entitlement for Keystone subscriptions aimed at European Economic Area customers with regional compliance and data-residency requirements. Nair said the offering will be available in early November for France and Germany, followed by broader availability later.
Mahesh Thiagarajan, executive vice president of Oracle Cloud Infrastructure at Oracle, said Oracle and NetApp are partnering to bring ONTAP to OCI. He said OCI File Storage and NetApp ONTAP will soon enable customers to run business-critical file-storage workloads in OCI using ONTAP tools, APIs and automation.
Thomas Kurian, CEO of Google Cloud, said Google Cloud NetApp Volumes supports enterprise workloads, agentic workloads and retrieval-augmented generation inferencing. He also said NetApp storage solutions are now embedded natively in Google Distributed Cloud, supporting air-gapped sovereign environments for Google AI models.
Scott Guthrie, executive vice president of Microsoft Cloud, said Microsoft and NetApp continue to help customers bring ONTAP workloads to Azure and run demanding workloads through Azure NetApp Files.
NetApp introduces Novus for AI factories
The event's largest announcement was NetApp Novus, a new disaggregated architecture intended for accelerated computing environments, large AI factories and GPU clusters exceeding 100,000 GPUs.
Kurian said Novus is designed to independently scale storage components and assimilate data across tens of thousands of systems into a single namespace. NetApp said the architecture is designed to deliver up to 100 TB per second of performance and a zettabyte-scale file system, claims the company characterized as first-of-their-kind capabilities.
Arindam Banerjee, NetApp's Chief Platform and Technology Officer, said Novus uses federation to combine multiple storage clusters into one namespace, with throughput increasing as clusters are added. The architecture uses standard pNFS and Flex Files protocols, he said, allowing use of the stock Linux kernel rather than requiring a proprietary client or kernel module.
Banerjee said Novus separates metadata services into independently scalable protocol, state and catalog planes, addressing metadata bottlenecks that can arise when AI workloads combine high-volume data reads and writes with extensive metadata operations. Novus data servers will run ONTAP, he added, extending NetApp's existing data integrity, resilience, security, isolation and quality-of-service capabilities to the new architecture.
Kurian said the announcements reflect NetApp's effort to help customers build intelligent data infrastructure that can transform enterprise data into usable knowledge for AI systems and agents.
NetApp, Inc develops intelligent data infrastructure and data management solutions for enterprises, service providers, and government organizations. The company helps customers store, manage, protect, and access data across on-premises environments, private clouds, public clouds, and hybrid multicloud infrastructures.
Its portfolio includes enterprise storage systems, all-flash arrays, cloud-connected storage, object storage, and data management software. NetApp's offerings include the ONTAP data management operating system, AFF and ASA storage systems, StorageGRID object storage, and BlueXP, a platform designed to help customers manage data and storage resources across multiple environments.

NetApp (NTAP) Acquires AI Storage Software Firm To Expand AI Infrastructure
NetApp (NasdaqGS:NTAP) disclosed plans to acquire UK-based PEAK:AIO, a provider of high-performance storage software for AI workloads.
The deal is expected to add advanced metadata capabilities and a parallel file system to NetApp's existing data infrastructure portfolio.
Management highlighted that PEAK:AIO's technology is aimed at customers running large GPU clusters and enterprise-scale AI solutions.
NetApp's move to acquire PEAK:AIO is worth weighing alongside the rest of our findings on the business. Our analysis turns up 1 warning sign for NetApp as well.
You can also look across a wider group of peers by exploring 87 AI infrastructure stocks.
NasdaqGS:NTAP Earnings & Revenue Growth as at Sep 2026
NetApp runs enterprise data software, systems, and services across regions including the US, Europe, and Asia Pacific, so acquiring PEAK:AIO fits its push to serve customers that are scaling AI workloads on top of existing storage infrastructure.
3 things going right for NetApp that this headline doesn't cover.
How the PEAK:AIO deal plugs into the NetApp AI storage story
NetApp's narrative revolves around AI and hybrid cloud workloads driving demand for its subscription-heavy storage platform, so buying PEAK:AIO speaks directly to that bet on higher-value, AI-ready services.
"Accelerating adoption of AI and analytics workloads across industries is driving demand for unified, high-performance, and scalable data infrastructure, with NetApp securing over 125 AI wins in Q1...
See how the full story points towards a $194 fair value for NetApp.
This acquisition leans into the part of the story that says AI and hybrid cloud demand can push more customers onto NetApp's integrated, subscription-based stack. PEAK:AIO's software focus lines up with Keystone and cloud services, which ties into the thesis that a richer services mix can support recurring revenue and margin resilience against rivals such as Dell or HPE.
The move does not address every concern, though. Analysts already flag pressure from hyperscaler partnerships and the shift away from traditional on-prem hardware. Absorbing PEAK:AIO adds execution risk around product integration and go-to-market focus, especially as competition from cloud-native storage providers remains intense.
The takeaway is that the same PEAK:AIO news can look like a smart AI storage accelerator or a fresh source of complexity, depending on which NetApp narrative a reader leans toward.

NetApp Recognizes Winners of 2026 North America Partner Awards
Thu, October 1, 2026 at 5:00 AM PDT 7 min read
NetApp commends partners for success in helping deliver NetApp solutions and services that address customer needs and industry trends
SAN JOSE, Calif., October 01, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--NetApp® (NASDAQ: NTAP), the Intelligent Data Infrastructure company, today announced at NetApp INSIGHT 2026 the winners of its North America Partner Awards for Fiscal Year 2026 (FY'26). NetApp's strategic partnerships aid in providing NetApp products and solutions to solve the business challenges of their joint customers.
The North America Partner Award winners have been instrumental in helping customers to build an Intelligent Data Infrastructure through the NetApp Platform, that can securely evolve and scale with their needs by driving sales of NetApp's solutions and services. Each winning partner has demonstrated a thorough understanding of the NetApp portfolio and has proven their ability to leverage NetApp's innovative solutions and services to give customers the confidence they need to overcome today's biggest technology challenges.
"Now more than ever, we must empower customers with AI-ready data that is secure by default and built for hybrid environments so they can achieve their business outcomes," said Alvaro Celis, Senior Vice President, Chief Commercial, Partner and Ecosystem Officer at NetApp. "This year's FY26 NetApp North America Partner Award winners exemplify innovation and transformation in the AI era. They helped customers solve data-readiness challenges by using the NetApp Platform to access, manage, and activate data across hybrid multicloud environments—enabling them to tackle demanding tasks and solve complex problems. On behalf of NetApp, congratulations to all this year's winners on their well-earned success."
North America Partner Award Winners for NetApp FY'26
North America Partner of the Year: Recognizing overall NetApp FY'26 revenue, services capabilities, net-new account wins, and top rankings across product categories.
Distributor of the Year: Recognizing the distributor that drives significant year-over-year (YoY) growth in their NetApp partner ecosystem while exhibiting demonstrated value in operations, sales and technical enablement, marketing, and financial services.
Winner: Arrow Enterprise Computing Solutions Inc.
Growth Partner of the Year: Recognizing the ability to generate significant YoY growth in NetApp revenue across the portfolio.
Flash Partner of the Year: Recognizing overall FY'26 flash revenue, significant YoY growth, and strategic account wins.
Winner: ePlus Inc.
New Account Acquisition Partner of the Year: Recognizing the highest number of net-new accounts to NetApp with focused sales efforts on helping customers achieve digital transformation with NetApp solutions.
NetApp Keystone® Partner of the Year: Recognizing a strategic sales and marketing approach to driving significant growth of NetApp Keystone.
AI Partner of the Year: Recognized for exceptional AI business performance, customer impact, and leadership in scaling AI solutions globally.
AI Go-to-Market Partner of the Year: Recognizing acceleration of AI adoption through innovative customer engagement, seller activation, and a differentiated AI go-to-market strategy.
Cloud Partner of the Year: Recognizing overall FY'26 cloud data services revenue and deploying a focused cloud digital transformation strategy that aligns with the NetApp cloud vision.
Canada Partner of the Year: Recognizing overall NetApp FY'26 revenue and alignment to the NetApp strategy in the Canadian market.

NetApp Q1 Beat and Raised Guidance Put AI Storage Growth in Focus
NetApp, Inc. NTAP opened fiscal 2027 with revenue and earnings well above expectations, while management materially raised its full-year outlook. The quarter sharpened the investment focus on whether AI-related storage demand is lifting the company's underlying growth rate.
Flash, Public Cloud and broader modernization demand all contributed to the advance. The next test is whether that momentum can persist as product mix pressures gross margin and customer purchasing patterns create tougher comparisons later in the year.
NetApp's Q1 Beat Resets the FY2027 Baseline
Fiscal first-quarter revenues rose 29.9% year over year to $2.025 billion, topping the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 9.9%. Non-GAAP earnings increased 66.5% to $2.58 per share and exceeded the consensus mark by 21.1%.
The quarter included an extra week that contributed about $65 million to revenues, mainly in support and Public Cloud. Even after adjusting for that benefit, revenues increased 26%, indicating that the beat was not solely a calendar effect.
NTAP's Flash and Cloud Mix Drives the Surprise
All-flash array revenues jumped 46.6% to a record $1.309 billion, while Public Cloud revenues increased 28% to a record $206 million. Public Cloud still grew 19% excluding the extra week. Together, all-flash and Public Cloud represented 75% of quarterly net revenues. NetApp also added about 350 AI and data lake modernization deals, with larger deal sizes as customers moved from pilots to production.
Competition remains active around the same AI data opportunity. Dell Technologies Inc. DELL reported record fiscal second-quarter 2027 storage revenue of $4.9 billion, up 26%. Hewlett Packard Enterprise Company HPE is expanding HPE Alletra Storage MP X10000 with native file storage alongside object storage for AI data pipelines, keeping pressure on storage vendors to sustain product differentiation.
NetApp raised fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $7.975-$8.225 billion. At the $8.1 billion midpoint, the outlook implies 17% year-over-year growth and is $650 million above the midpoint of the prior guidance.
Non-GAAP earnings guidance increased to $9.73-$10.03 per share, with the $9.88 midpoint representing 22% growth. Management also lifted non-GAAP operating margin guidance to 30.3%-31.3%, suggesting that operating leverage can remain meaningful if demand holds.
NetApp, Inc. price-eps-surprise | NetApp, Inc. Quote
NTAP's Margin Outlook Tests the Quality of Growth
The stronger top-line mix has a cost. First-quarter non-GAAP gross margin slipped 50 basis points year over year to 70.6%, while product gross margin fell 150 basis points sequentially to 54.6% as component costs rose. Product revenues were 49% of total revenues, up from 42% a year earlier, contributing to the consolidated margin pressure.
For fiscal 2027, non-GAAP gross margin is expected at 68.1%-69.1%, reflecting a richer product mix. Free cash flow fell 35.3% year over year to $401 million in the first quarter, while accelerated purchasing by some large customers can make quarterly growth and cash conversion less even.
NetApp's Momentum Signals Stay Constructive
The earnings event supports a higher near-term growth baseline, but durability still depends on continued AI deal conversion, cloud expansion and efficient margin execution. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for earnings in the current fiscal year has increased 2.5% over the past four weeks, adding support to the near-term setup.
NTAP currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), a favorable short-term signal tied to earnings estimate revisions, and a Momentum Score of A. Its Growth Score of C, Value Score of D and VGM Score of C are less supportive.

First Quarter of Fiscal Year 2027 Business Highlights
NetApp announced the release of StorageGRID 12.1, designed to help customers scale AI and other modern workloads with a federated global namespace, improving how data is accessed, processed, and managed across distributed environments to support AI data pipelines.
NetApp announced new capabilities to NetApp Trident software 26.06 that helps Kubernetes platform teams scale workloads, while adding smarter volume placement, non-disruptive iSCSI volume rebalancing, expanded cloud support, and deeper integration for OpenShift Virtualization migrations.
NetApp announced new data management capabilities optimized for Red Hat OpenShift that enable advanced levels of resilience and scale for virtualized environments, on-premises and in the cloud.

NetApp announced the general availability of Azure NetApp Files Object REST API to eliminate complex data pipelines and enable direct access to AI capabilities through standardized interfaces.

NetApp announced the general availability of Azure NetApp Files migration assistant to accelerate and simplify migrations of business-critical applications and data to Azure.

NetApp announced an expanded collaboration with Cisco to strengthen defense-in-depth strategies for customers with the new NetApp Splunk Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR) playbook.

NetApp and SK Telecom announced the completion of a joint proof of concept, using NetApp AFX systems with SK Telecom’s Petasus AI Cloud, demonstrating a solution that enables enterprises to scale AI infrastructure in virtualized environments while maintaining high performance.
NetApp and Okestro signed a strategic partnership agreement to jointly develop integrated enterprise AI and disaster recovery infrastructure.
NetApp announced a strategic partnership with Tata Consultancy Services to better help organizations discover, classify, and govern data across locations, reduce the impact of cyber-attacks, speed up recovery times, and provide insights on sensitive data locations and permissions.
NetApp announced its acquisition of DataPelago, Inc., to further enable computing where data is created and stored, accelerating demanding workloads while improving infrastructure efficiency at scale.
NetApp appointed Alvaro Celis as Chief Partner and Ecosystem Officer to lead partner ecosystems, modernize incentive programs, improve partner satisfaction, and drive growth.
NetApp CEO, George Kurian, was named to CRN’s 25 Most Influential Executives of 2026 list, emphasizing his leadership in data storage amid the age of cloud and AI.
NetApp’s AI Data Engine was named as a finalist in CRN’s 2026 Tech Innovator Awards, noting its ability to transform massive unstructured data estates into always-fresh, AI-ready assets with enterprise-grade security, compliance, and operational efficiency.

NetApp was named to Time Magazine’s Best Companies of 2026 list, ranking 271 out of 1,000 organizations.
NetApp was named as one of the Best Companies to Work For by U.S. News, highlighting its top work environment.

NetApp Usage of Non-GAAP Financial Information
To supplement NetApp’s condensed consolidated financial statement information presented in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States (GAAP), NetApp provides investors with certain non-GAAP measures, including, but not limited to, historical non-GAAP gross margins, non-GAAP gross profit, non-GAAP operating income, non-GAAP operating margins, non-GAAP net income, non-GAAP effective tax rate, free cash flow, billings, and historical and projected non-GAAP earnings per share.
NetApp believes that the presentation of its non-GAAP measures, when shown in conjunction with the corresponding GAAP measures, provides useful information to investors and management regarding financial and business trends relating to its financial condition and results of operations. Non-GAAP financial measures are used to: (1) measure company performance against historical results, (2) facilitate comparisons to our competitors’ operating results, and (3) allow greater transparency with respect to information used by management in financial and operational decision making.
NetApp believes that the presentation of non-GAAP gross margins, non-GAAP gross profit, non-GAAP operating income, non-GAAP operating margins, non-GAAP effective tax rate, non-GAAP net income, and non-GAAP earnings per share data provides investors with supplemental metrics that assist in understanding current results and future prospects, earnings and profitability that are complementary to GAAP metrics. GAAP earnings per share and non-GAAP earnings per share are calculated using the net income divided by the diluted number of shares for the applicable period.
NetApp believes that the presentation of free cash flow, which it defines as the net cash provided by operating activities less cash used to acquire property and equipment, to be a liquidity measure that provides useful information to investors and management because it reflects cash that can be used to, among other things, invest in its business, make strategic acquisitions, repurchase common stock, and pay dividends on its common stock. As free cash flow is not a measure of liquidity calculated in accordance with GAAP, free cash flow should be considered in addition to, but not as a substitute for, the analysis provided in the statement of cash flows.
NetApp approximates billings by adding net revenues as reported on our Condensed Consolidated Statements of Operations for the period to the change in total deferred revenue as reported on our Condensed Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows for the same period. Billings is a performance measure that NetApp believes provides useful information to investors and management because it approximates the amounts under purchase orders received by us during a given period that have been billed.
NetApp excludes the following items from its non-GAAP measures when applicable:
A. Amortization of intangible assets. NetApp records amortization of intangible assets that were acquired in connection with its business combinations. The amortization of intangible assets varies depending on the level of acquisition activity. Management finds it useful to exclude these charges to assess the appropriate level of various operating expenses to assist in budgeting, planning and forecasting future periods and in measuring operational performance.
B. Stock-based compensation expenses. NetApp excludes stock-based compensation expenses from its non-GAAP measures primarily because the amount can fluctuate based on variables unrelated to the performance of the underlying business. While management views stock-based compensation as a key element of our employee retention and long-term incentives, we do not view it as an expense to be used in evaluating operational performance in any given period.
C. Litigation settlements. NetApp may periodically incur charges or benefits related to litigation settlements. NetApp excludes these charges and benefits, when significant, because it does not believe they are reflective of ongoing business and operating results.

Chief executive Ryan Cohen disclosed a $26 million purchase of GameStop (NYSE:GME | GME Price Prediction) shares in a regulatory filing earlier this week, putting his own money behind the retailer at recent levels. GameStop stock is down 8% to $23.11 in morning trading, a drop that still leaves the shares up 29% over the past month.
The VanEck Video Gaming and eSports ETF (NASDAQ:ESPO) is down 0.8%, a much softer dip for a fund that holds GameStop among its gaming names. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is up 0.11% to $768, leaving the broad market essentially steady. GameStop stock is falling far harder than both funds, which keeps the pressure centered on its own crowded positioning.
Ryan Cohen’s filing showed he bought roughly 1.1 million GameStop shares, and the stock rose once the disclosure became public. That purchase is several sessions old, which means GameStop shares are trading on how holders handle the gain it produced.
The drop in GameStop stock reflects profit taking after that sustained run. Holders who followed Cohen into the shares are booking part of their gains, and the modest declines in the gaming fund and the S&P 500 fund show that selling hasn’t spread beyond this one name.
Within the VanEck fund, GameStop shares made up 4.3% of net assets as of June 30, a mid-sized weighting in a portfolio led by larger game publishers. The rest of the portfolio leans on names such as Capcom, Konami and Bandai Namco, and that mix is posting only a softer decline. That gap shows the selling in GameStop stock is specific to the retailer.
The SPDR fund’s slip is far too small to explain a move of this scale in GameStop shares. Crowded positioning in GameStop stock, built during the monthly run, can amplify an unwind once holders start taking profits, and the stock’s own behavior is carrying the loss.
GameStop’s most recent quarterly profit got a lift from its stake in eBay (NASDAQ:EBAY), a holding of roughly 43.4 million shares valued at $4.9 billion. Earlier this year, GameStop made an unsolicited bid for eBay, which eBay rejected. The retailer has also reduced debt by swapping bonds for company stock, a path that avoided paying out cash. eBay stock is up 0.47% to $108.34.
Weighing Cohen’s Signal Against the Pullback
The optimistic argument for GameStop begins with who bought the shares. A chief executive putting personal money into the shares at recent levels is the least ambiguous signal an insider can send, and the purchase ties Cohen’s fortunes more closely to those of other holders. GameStop also lists its dependence on Ryan Cohen among its risk factors, emphasizing how central he is to the story.
Timing is the problem for GameStop. The stock has given back part of what it gained on the news, so the signal has been priced and then partly reversed. GameStop’s latest quarterly report also flags the concentration of its investment portfolio in eBay common stock as a risk, tying part of the company’s value to a single outside holding.
Whether the monthly gain in GameStop stock holds without a fresh reason to own the shares is what these figures don’t settle. Cohen’s buy, the eBay position and the debt swaps are all known quantities, and none of them is new information. That leaves GameStop shares leaning on sentiment until the company offers its next update.
It is worth watching for any new disclosure from GameStop on its eBay stake or on insider buying, since either could give the shares another reason to move. A second purchase from Cohen would reinforce the original signal, while a quiet stretch could let profit taking run further.
Swings of this magnitude in GameStop stock reward discipline. Anyone adding GameStop shares on the drop ought to stay small, and holders already sitting on gains should size their exposure with that volatility in mind. Setting an exit level in advance can keep a sharp reversal from turning into an oversized hit to their portfolio.
Stocks that fall this hard against a steady market can reverse quickly in either direction. For GameStop, the insider purchase confirms conviction at the top of the company, and the next test for the stock is whether its monthly advance lasts without a new catalyst.

When we hear stories about large companies, it can feel like they were people from a different world from the very beginning. They had amazing technology, massive amounts of capital, and a clear path to success. We assume that's why they were able to do it.
However, I feel that by looking only at the finished product, we distance ourselves from the actions we can take today. This time, I would like to think about what we should verify in a small business, starting from the origins of eBay.
The entrance to a large market was an individual's trading experiment
The founder of eBay is Pierre Omidyar. In his biography submitted to the SEC, it is explained that he started it as a sole proprietorship in September 1995 and incorporated it in May 1996. You cannot equate the current size of the company with its form at the time of founding.Founder and Management Biography from eBay's 2006 SEC Filing
The initial site was named AuctionWeb. In a letter from the founder in February 1996, he noted that since launching on Labor Day of the previous year, usage had spread beyond his imagination, and he had come to feel that it was a major experiment in testing commercial transactions on the Internet.Pierre Omidyar's Founder Letter dated February 26, 1996
What attracts me to this is the fact that a grand success story wasn't already complete at the start. First, you create a place for transactions. People come there. Interactions occur. By watching those reactions, you gradually see what is needed next.
Of course, just because you know how eBay started doesn't mean that doing the same thing will lead to the same result. The times and the competition are different. However, we can also re-question whether we need to keep increasing our preparations before verifying someone's reaction.
Starting small is different from starting sloppily. Even if you are handling just one product, you still need to confirm its condition, provide a description, determine how to deliver it, and commit to communication. Scaling down is not about letting go of that responsibility, but about creating a scope that you can verify yourself until the end.
Before asking "Did it sell?", what do you want to verify?
For example, suppose someone starting an overseas sales business first researches a single product. If they decide at this point that "if it doesn't sell in a week, I'm not cut out for this," they will overlook what they could have learned. Are they failing to use the words buyers are searching for? Is the condition not being conveyed? Do the price and shipping terms not match? You cannot understand the cause from the result alone.
If it were me, I would first write down just one thing I want to verify with this action. For example, "Can the scratches on this product be conveyed to the other party through photos and descriptions alone?" For that purpose, you can not only increase the number of photos but also have a third party look at them and ask where it is difficult to make a judgment.
The action of generating sales and the action of understanding the state in which you can generate sales are not always the same. If you think about this separately, I think the pain of feeling like your entire self is being evaluated by a single reaction will decrease a little.
I also want to decide the scope of the trial in advance. The time I can use, the amount of money I can put into inventory, the place where I can store items, and the time I can spend answering inquiries. If you expand your experiment to the point of breaking your daily life or commitments, you may find yourself unable to continue before you get any results.
This is not a story about making your dreams small. It is a story about choosing a step that the current you can take responsibility for, in order to continue while protecting the things you love. Precisely because you have resolve, you want to think about a form that allows you to continue.
Turn today's step into a record that allows for the next judgment
What you can do today is make a single memo about the product or service you want to test. "Who do I want to help and with what?" "How is that person doing now?" "Where am I verifying this time?" If you can write these three things in your own words, it becomes easier to determine the priority of your preparations.
After executing, separate what you did from the other party's reaction and keep a record. I changed the description. I retook the photos. There was an inquiry. How many hours did it take to respond? If you keep a record of what actually happened, not just your own impressions, you can choose where to change next.
The less reaction you get, the more you might want to change everything at once. But if you change the product, the price, and the description, you won't know which change was relevant. If it were me, I would fix things one by one, starting from the parts where the reason for review is clear. Of course, problems related to safety or misdescription are handled first.
Before you start, I think it's good to decide when you will look back. The purpose of setting a period is not to decide quickly whether it is a success or a failure. It is to verify what you have learned and what you still do not know using the time you have decided upon. Even if there is no reaction, you can specifically leave behind where to look and the order in which to try things.
Before deciding to "increase products because they aren't selling," you can return to those notes. If you can't keep up with managing the current number, increasing them isn't necessarily the answer. I want to be able to choose the next step based on what I've learned, rather than on a whim.
Another thing I want you to keep track of is what was inconvenient for the customer. Even if you think you've explained it well enough, it might be too long for the other person, or the necessary information might be buried at the end. When you're at a small stage, it should be easier to fix those inconveniences with your own hands.
What I want to cultivate in my business is not just the single event of a sale. It's about the people involved being able to make their own decisions next time, and being able to move forward with more peace of mind than before. I believe that this accumulation is what gives meaning to running a business.
It would be a waste to use the history of eBay only to look at an amazing company. Even for those of us who aren't big yet, we can take action today to reduce one inconvenience. Let's leave that step behind in a way that leads to tomorrow's decisions.

Ryan Cohen wrote a personal check for a million shares of his own company. The filing dated September 10, 2026 shows the purchase at $20.3759 per share, and a director bought the same day. The stock settled the most recent session at $24.04, up 5.62%.
GameStop (NYSE:GME | GME Price Prediction) sales keep sliding while a proposed takeover of eBay (NASDAQ:EBAY), a business several times its size, sits on the risk-factor page of the last 8-K. Open-market purchases with personal money are the most informative signal any insider can send. A chief executive writing a check for tens of millions while quarterly revenue falls almost 19% is likely seeing something the market hasn’t priced in yet.
Three directors bought in the same window: Lawrence Cheng, 55,000 shares at $18.7992 on September 8, James Grube, 10,255 at $19.12 on September 9, and Alain Attal, 5,000 at $20.00 on September 10.
Insider sells have a dozen reasons. Insider buys have one. A purchase at a higher price than the last one carries even more information.
The Q2 FY2027 8-K, filed September 8, 2026, discloses approximately 43.4 million shares of eBay common stock valued at approximately $4.9 billion and continues to reference the proposed acquisition of eBay in forward-looking risk factors.
The word that matters is proposed. The bid has never been formally withdrawn, and the company still flags that it may not be completed.
Revenue in the most recent quarter came in at $790.2 million, down 18.7% year over year, yet operating income jumped to $160.2 million, up 141.27%. Gross margin expanded to 43.7% from 29.1%.
Collectibles hit $356.3 million, up 57%, and now make up 45.1% of net sales. Video games fell to $263.2 million from $494.6 million.
However, I’d ignore the headline net income. It was flattered by a $166.3 million derivative gain tied to eBay and dinged by a $75 million loss on digital assets.
Balance Sheet, Guidance, and the Trigger
Against a market cap of $12.13 billion, GameStop carries $4.85 billion in cash and a $4.9 billion eBay position. A meaningful share of the equity value sits in marketable securities rather than in store operations.
Management raised the fiscal 2026 Adjusted EBITDA outlook to in excess of $650 million from in excess of $600 million. The trigger is a formal withdrawal of the eBay bid, a definitive agreement, or another Cohen buy at a price above $20.3759.
Bull: a chief executive spending real money on his own stock in a coordinated cluster with directors, a collectibles category growing fast enough to reshape the mix, record operating income for the period, and an investment portfolio no other specialty retailer can match.
Bear: total sales are still falling, the crypto position introduces volatility unrelated to the business, and the eBay bid may quietly evaporate into a passive stake that never becomes a deal.
The deciding variable is whether collectibles growth can outrun the legacy business’s decline before the market decides the eBay stake is just an expensive hedge fund position wrapped in a retailer.

What you need to know to avoid losses on your first overseas purchase
As I continue to list items on eBay, I sometimes hear from Japanese buyers who say they use Sekaimon even though they suspect it might actually be cheaper to buy directly on eBay.
As someone who has been on the selling side of eBay for a long time, I have realized through my transactions that the experience of receiving an item can change significantly depending on how you buy it, even for the same product.
In this article, I will organize how eBay and Sekaimon work and what the differences are.
By the time you finish reading, you should have the information you need to decide which one you should choose.
What is the fundamental difference between eBay and Sekaimon?
eBay is an auction and flea market platform where sellers from all over the world list items directly and buyers purchase them directly.
On the other hand, Sekaimon is a service that allows you to view and purchase eBay listings in Japanese, and handles everything from the purchase to international shipping and customs clearance to Japan. service.
In other words, Sekaimon is not eBay itself, but is positioned as an intermediary service that makes eBay products easier to use from Japan.
One reason this difference is hard to understand is that the products displayed on the Sekaimon purchase screen are actually items listed by eBay sellers.
There are many cases where the entry point for buying is different, but the source of the product itself is the same.
Even from my perspective as a seller listing items on eBay, there are actually not many situations where I am conscious of whether a buyer is using Sekaimon or buying directly through eBay.
However, because fees, supported languages, and shipping mechanisms differ significantly, the experience will change depending on which one the buyer chooses.
A typical case is assuming that Sekaimon is an official eBay service.
In reality, it is an independent intermediary service operated by a separate company, and its fee structure and support are also different.
Another is simply comparing the displayed price on Sekaimon to see if it is higher or lower than buying directly on eBay.
Since Sekaimon's fees include international shipping and customs procedures, it is easy to misjudge the actual profit or loss if you compare them without understanding the breakdown of the displayed amount.
I have also had several opportunities to explain this difference in mechanism when buyers asked me about pricing.
In the end, which one is right for you?
Based on what we have covered so far, the answer to the question of whether you should use eBay or Sekaimon comes down to the difference in priority between choosing based solely on low cost versus choosing based on peace of mind and convenience.
Using eBay directly is suitable for those who are comfortable with English correspondence and want to handle everything themselves, including direct communication with sellers and price negotiations.
On the other hand, intermediary services like Sekaimon are suitable for those who are uneasy about communicating in English and would rather prioritize the peace of mind provided by Japanese support and proxy services, even if it means paying some fees.
The key criteria for your decision are how much you can handle in terms of English correspondence, how you compare the total costs including fees, and which support you can rely on in the event of a problem—these three points.
These are not matters of special knowledge, but things anyone can judge if they correctly understand how the systems work.
So, how should you actually compare them and how should you use them differently?
From here on, rather than general principles, you will need actual fee simulations and the specific procedures for how to use them.
Many of the questions regarding "what is the difference between eBay and Sekaimon" can be resolved once you understand the division of roles between the two.

The practical guide for that is explained in this article, complete with specific fee simulations.

Should You Buy eBay Stock For Its Cash?
eBay's (EBAY) free cash flow is 5.2% of its market value, against 4.6% for the median S&P 500 company. A stock usually offers more cash for its price than most for one of two reasons. Investors either underrate the business or expect its cash to shrink. A buyer needs to know whether eBay's cash is underrated or about to shrink.
eBay's free cash flow was $2.4 billion over the last twelve months, up from $1.4 billion a year earlier. Free cash flow is the cash left after a company pays its costs and funds its investment.
As a shareholder, you own a share of that cash whether or not eBay pays it out. Every $10,000 of eBay stock comes with about $520 of free cash flow a year. When investors value that cash more highly, the share price tends to follow. The effect is stronger when the cash is growing.
eBay earns revenue on the sales that pass through its marketplace. The revenue comes from fees, advertising and shipping services. In the second quarter of 2026, eBay kept 14% of the value of goods sold as revenue. The marketplace needs little investment. eBay spent $0.6 billion on capital investment out of the $3.0 billion its operations brought in over the last twelve months.
eBay's free cash flow was positive throughout the last three years, but it did not hold steady. Three years ago it was $2.4 billion, the same as today. It fell to $1.5 billion the following year before recovering.
eBay owes little against that cash. Net debt, which is debt minus cash, was $3.8 billion on its latest reported balance sheet. That debt is 8.1% of eBay's market value. eBay's operating profit is 9.9 times its interest bill.
Why Does eBay Stock Yield More Than Most?
eBay stock yields more partly because the price appears to assume its growth is slowing. The stock lost 7.5% over the past three months, while the S&P 500 returned 2.7%.
Management's own forecast shows a slowdown. Adjusted earnings per share grew 17% in the second quarter of 2026. For the third quarter, management guided growth of 1% to 5%.
On its August 5, 2026 call, management explained the slowdown from the second quarter to the third. Most of it comes from harder comparisons with last year, management said. A year ago, eBay had the benefit of the launch of its U.S. Klarna partnership and of triple-digit growth in Pokémon. Both make comparisons in 2026 tougher.
eBay also bought Depop, a resale business, for $1.4 billion in cash on July 30, 2026. Management expected two effects from Depop in the third quarter. Depop would add about 2.5 points to currency-neutral growth in the value of goods sold. The purchase would also take 3 to 4 points off adjusted operating income growth.
eBay's operating margin, its operating profit per dollar of revenue, has already slipped. The margin was 20.5% over the last twelve months, down from 21.3% a year earlier. Even so, management raised its full-year outlook on the August 5 call. Management also expects Depop to add to adjusted operating income in 2028.
Watch eBay's Earnings Growth Against Its Guide
Adjusted earnings growth above the 1% to 5% that management guided would be a sign that eBay's cash is still rising. Growth at the low end, with a lower operating margin, would be a sign of cash levelling off.
eBay's free cash flow is back at its level of three years ago. The risk is that eBay's cash stops rising as its earnings growth slows.
eBay can carry its debt: its operating profit is 9.9 times its interest bill. The open question is growth. The third-quarter 2026 results will show whether eBay keeps growing through harder comparisons and the cost of Depop.

As of September 24, 2026, eBay no longer permits sellers to list standalone airbags or airbag inflators. Steering wheel airbag covers are included in the prohibition as well.
The marketplace says the decision followed a comprehensive review of the risks these products can pose to users. The change arrives amid heightened scrutiny of dangerous replacement airbag components that have made their way into vehicles in the United States.
Recent findings from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration illustrate just how serious the consequences can be. The agency says one particular type of defective replacement inflator has now been connected to 11 deaths and three severe injuries.

eBay's new policy applies across its airbag category and prohibits any seller from offering airbags or inflators. Sellers were instructed to remove affected active, scheduled, and draft listings by September 24, with eBay saying it would remove remaining listings itself.
There are some exceptions for related components that don't actually contain an airbag or inflator. Outside the United States, items such as airbag control units, crash sensors, diagnostic modules, and passenger sensors can continue to be listed, while U.S. sales of those parts are restricted to currently pre-approved sellers.
Trying to relist prohibited equipment could result in selling restrictions. eBay says listings removed as part of the policy change won't negatively affect a seller's compliance history.
Defective Replacement Inflators Have Killed 11 People
The timing is notable given NHTSA's ongoing warnings about dangerous replacement airbags. In April, the agency took the unusual step of banning the sale and importation of certain frontal driver airbag inflators marked DTN60DB after determining that they contained a safety-related defect.
Instead of operating normally during a collision, the defective inflators can rupture and propel metal fragments into the passenger compartment. NHTSA's latest figures link them to 11 deaths and three severe injuries across 14 crashes in the United States.
The agency says the affected vehicles had previously received replacement driver-side frontal airbag inflators. Airbags rely on an extremely rapid deployment process to protect occupants during a collision. NHTSA estimates frontal airbags saved more than 50,000 lives over a 30-year period, illustrating just how valuable the technology can be when everything works properly.
The problem is that determining the history and authenticity of a replacement component purchased online isn't always straightforward. NHTSA recommends that owners whose vehicles previously experienced an airbag deployment have replacement equipment inspected by a reputable mechanic, particularly if the repair wasn't performed by the manufacturer's dealership.
Losing easy access to used airbags on eBay might be inconvenient for some repairers and enthusiasts. Still, when the part sitting inches from your face is designed to explosively deploy during a crash, this is one online bargain that's probably better left alone.

Peggy Alford, SVP, Chief Financial Officer, reported the disposition of 2,716 shares of eBay Inc.(EBAY +0.48%) on Sept. 15, 2026, according to a SEC Form 4 filing.
Post-transaction shares (directly held)26,188
Transaction value based on SEC Form 4 weighted average sale price ($108.03); post-transaction value based on Sept. 15, 2026, market close ($108.03).
What was the specific context of this disposition?
The transaction was non-discretionary. It was executed automatically to cover tax liabilities associated with the vesting of restricted stock units. This activity occurred independently of any discretionary trading decision by the executive.
How does this impact the executive's total equity exposure?
While 2,716 shares were withheld for taxes, the executive continues to hold 26,188 direct shares, representing a 0.006% ownership interest. Alford also holds 34,540 derivative securities, including vested and unvested awards.
What are the terms of the underlying equity awards?
The shares originated from restricted stock units subject to a four-year vesting schedule. According to the filing, these awards began vesting in June 2026, with further portions scheduled to vest quarterly.
What was the executive's total transaction activity in this filing?
The filing involved the exercise of 5,371 options, which were immediately converted into shares. Following this exercise and the subsequent tax withholding, the executive's total direct common stock position increased from 23,533 to 26,188 shares.
Share Price (as of market close 2026-09-17)$112.90
eBay operates a global e-commerce marketplace platform that enables buyers and sellers to list, discover, purchase, and transact across a diverse array of goods through its flagship website, mobile applications, and multiple sales channels.
The company generates revenue primarily through transaction fees, listing fees, and ancillary services provided to sellers and buyers utilizing its digital marketplace infrastructure.
eBay serves a broad customer base encompassing individual consumers, small businesses, and enterprises seeking to buy and sell merchandise across numerous product categories on a global scale.
eBay Inc. operates one of the world's largest e-commerce marketplaces, facilitating billions of dollars in gross merchandise volume annually across its diversified platform ecosystem. The company maintains a significant competitive advantage through its established network effects, extensive seller base, and integrated payment and logistics solutions. With approximately 12,300 employees and a market capitalization of $50.2 billion, eBay continues to serve as a critical infrastructure provider for digital commerce globally.
What this transaction means for investors
In a strange twist, Peggy Alford's sale of eBay shares may actually bolster the buy case for the consumer discretionary stock rather than undermining it.
Alford received stock options on a vesting schedule. With that, she sold some of her shares to meet tax liabilities. But amid the vesting and sale, her share count actually increased, as she retained some of the shares she bought. Consequently, she now owns 2,655 more common shares than before the transactions.
This looks like a sensible move. Its revenue for the first half of 2026 was $6.2 billion, 17% higher than in the same year-ago period. Additionally, the nearly $1.1 billion in net income during that time surged 23% higher over the same time frame. Consequently, the stock is higher by about 25% over the last year.

GameStop Tumbles 8% Despite Ryan Cohen’s $26M Insider Buy; eBay Ticks Up
Ryan Cohen just put $26 million of his own money into GameStop shares, yet the stock is sliding hard anyway. The question now is whether that insider conviction holds the monthly rally together or profit takers win the argument.
Published September 25, 2026, 10:56am ET · 4 min read
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
The exterior of a GameStop store, symbolizing the company's unexpected financial strength and potential for strategic acquisitions. © GameStop Logo Sign - Vallejo - California (CC BY 2.0) by Will Buckner
Chief executive Ryan Cohen disclosed a $26 million purchase of GameStop (NYSE:GME | GME Price Prediction) shares in a regulatory filing earlier this week, putting his own money behind the retailer at recent levels. GameStop stock is down 8% to $23.11 in morning trading, a drop that still leaves the shares up 29% over the past month.
The VanEck Video Gaming and eSports ETF (NASDAQ:ESPO) is down 0.8%, a much softer dip for a fund that holds GameStop among its gaming names. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is up 0.11% to $768, leaving the broad market essentially steady. GameStop stock is falling far harder than both funds, which keeps the pressure centered on its own crowded positioning.
Ryan Cohen’s filing showed he bought roughly 1.1 million GameStop shares, and the stock rose once the disclosure became public. That purchase is several sessions old, which means GameStop shares are trading on how holders handle the gain it produced.
The drop in GameStop stock reflects profit taking after that sustained run. Holders who followed Cohen into the shares are booking part of their gains, and the modest declines in the gaming fund and the S&P 500 fund show that selling hasn’t spread beyond this one name.
Within the VanEck fund, GameStop shares made up 4.3% of net assets as of June 30, a mid-sized weighting in a portfolio led by larger game publishers. The rest of the portfolio leans on names such as Capcom, Konami and Bandai Namco, and that mix is posting only a softer decline. That gap shows the selling in GameStop stock is specific to the retailer.
The SPDR fund’s slip is far too small to explain a move of this scale in GameStop shares. Crowded positioning in GameStop stock, built during the monthly run, can amplify an unwind once holders start taking profits, and the stock’s own behavior is carrying the loss.
GameStop’s most recent quarterly profit got a lift from its stake in eBay (NASDAQ:EBAY), a holding of roughly 43.4 million shares valued at $4.9 billion. Earlier this year, GameStop made an unsolicited bid for eBay, which eBay rejected. The retailer has also reduced debt by swapping bonds for company stock, a path that avoided paying out cash. eBay stock is up 0.47% to $108.34.
Weighing Cohen’s Signal Against the Pullback
The optimistic argument for GameStop begins with who bought the shares. A chief executive putting personal money into the shares at recent levels is the least ambiguous signal an insider can send, and the purchase ties Cohen’s fortunes more closely to those of other holders. GameStop also lists its dependence on Ryan Cohen among its risk factors, emphasizing how central he is to the story.
Timing is the problem for GameStop. The stock has given back part of what it gained on the news, so the signal has been priced and then partly reversed. GameStop’s latest quarterly report also flags the concentration of its investment portfolio in eBay common stock as a risk, tying part of the company’s value to a single outside holding.
Whether the monthly gain in GameStop stock holds without a fresh reason to own the shares is what these figures don’t settle. Cohen’s buy, the eBay position and the debt swaps are all known quantities, and none of them is new information. That leaves GameStop shares leaning on sentiment until the company offers its next update.
It is worth watching for any new disclosure from GameStop on its eBay stake or on insider buying, since either could give the shares another reason to move. A second purchase from Cohen would reinforce the original signal, while a quiet stretch could let profit taking run further.
Swings of this magnitude in GameStop stock reward discipline. Anyone adding GameStop shares on the drop ought to stay small, and holders already sitting on gains should size their exposure with that volatility in mind. Setting an exit level in advance can keep a sharp reversal from turning into an oversized hit to their portfolio.
Stocks that fall this hard against a steady market can reverse quickly in either direction. For GameStop, the insider purchase confirms conviction at the top of the company, and the next test for the stock is whether its monthly advance lasts without a new catalyst.

eBay started as a one-person experiment, too. What to value when starting small
Nemoto here!
When we hear stories about large companies, it can feel like they were people from a different world from the very beginning. They had amazing technology, massive amounts of capital, and a clear path to success. We assume that's why they were able to do it.
However, I feel that by looking only at the finished product, we distance ourselves from the actions we can take today. This time, I would like to think about what we should verify in a small business, starting from the origins of eBay.
The entrance to a large market was an individual's trading experiment
The founder of eBay is Pierre Omidyar. In his biography submitted to the SEC, it is explained that he started it as a sole proprietorship in September 1995 and incorporated it in May 1996. You cannot equate the current size of the company with its form at the time of founding.Founder and Management Biography from eBay's 2006 SEC Filing
The initial site was named AuctionWeb. In a letter from the founder in February 1996, he noted that since launching on Labor Day of the previous year, usage had spread beyond his imagination, and he had come to feel that it was a major experiment in testing commercial transactions on the Internet.Pierre Omidyar's Founder Letter dated February 26, 1996
What attracts me to this is the fact that a grand success story wasn't already complete at the start. First, you create a place for transactions. People come there. Interactions occur. By watching those reactions, you gradually see what is needed next.
Of course, just because you know how eBay started doesn't mean that doing the same thing will lead to the same result. The times and the competition are different. However, we can also re-question whether we need to keep increasing our preparations before verifying someone's reaction.
Starting small is different from starting sloppily. Even if you are handling just one product, you still need to confirm its condition, provide a description, determine how to deliver it, and commit to communication. Scaling down is not about letting go of that responsibility, but about creating a scope that you can verify yourself until the end.
Before asking "Did it sell?", what do you want to verify?
For example, suppose someone starting an overseas sales business first researches a single product. If they decide at this point that "if it doesn't sell in a week, I'm not cut out for this," they will overlook what they could have learned. Are they failing to use the words buyers are searching for? Is the condition not being conveyed? Do the price and shipping terms not match? You cannot understand the cause from the result alone.
If it were me, I would first write down just one thing I want to verify with this action. For example, "Can the scratches on this product be conveyed to the other party through photos and descriptions alone?" For that purpose, you can not only increase the number of photos but also have a third party look at them and ask where it is difficult to make a judgment.
The action of generating sales and the action of understanding the state in which you can generate sales are not always the same. If you think about this separately, I think the pain of feeling like your entire self is being evaluated by a single reaction will decrease a little.
I also want to decide the scope of the trial in advance. The time I can use, the amount of money I can put into inventory, the place where I can store items, and the time I can spend answering inquiries. If you expand your experiment to the point of breaking your daily life or commitments, you may find yourself unable to continue before you get any results.
This is not a story about making your dreams small. It is a story about choosing a step that the current you can take responsibility for, in order to continue while protecting the things you love. Precisely because you have resolve, you want to think about a form that allows you to continue.
Turn today's step into a record that allows for the next judgment
What you can do today is make a single memo about the product or service you want to test. "Who do I want to help and with what?" "How is that person doing now?" "Where am I verifying this time?" If you can write these three things in your own words, it becomes easier to determine the priority of your preparations.
After executing, separate what you did from the other party's reaction and keep a record. I changed the description. I retook the photos. There was an inquiry. How many hours did it take to respond? If you keep a record of what actually happened, not just your own impressions, you can choose where to change next.
The less reaction you get, the more you might want to change everything at once. But if you change the product, the price, and the description, you won't know which change was relevant. If it were me, I would fix things one by one, starting from the parts where the reason for review is clear. Of course, problems related to safety or misdescription are handled first.
Before you start, I think it's good to decide when you will look back. The purpose of setting a period is not to decide quickly whether it is a success or a failure. It is to verify what you have learned and what you still do not know using the time you have decided upon. Even if there is no reaction, you can specifically leave behind where to look and the order in which to try things.
Before deciding to "increase products because they aren't selling," you can return to those notes. If you can't keep up with managing the current number, increasing them isn't necessarily the answer. I want to be able to choose the next step based on what I've learned, rather than on a whim.
Another thing I want you to keep track of is what was inconvenient for the customer. Even if you think you've explained it well enough, it might be too long for the other person, or the necessary information might be buried at the end. When you're at a small stage, it should be easier to fix those inconveniences with your own hands.
What I want to cultivate in my business is not just the single event of a sale. It's about the people involved being able to make their own decisions next time, and being able to move forward with more peace of mind than before. I believe that this accumulation is what gives meaning to running a business.
It would be a waste to use the history of eBay only to look at an amazing company. Even for those of us who aren't big yet, we can take action today to reduce one inconvenience. Let's leave that step behind in a way that leads to tomorrow's decisions.

Blancco Donates Diagnostics and Data Erasure Software Licenses for Quick Ship’s eBay Live Charity Auction
All auction proceeds directly benefit Jonathan's Landing, a nonprofit that builds neuroinclusive housing and workforce pathways
Boston, MASSACHUSETTS, Sept. 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Blancco Technology Group, the industry standard in data erasure and mobile lifecycle solutions, today announced its participation in an eBay Live charity auction initiative led by its customer Quick Ship Brands, a certified reverse logistics, refurbishment, and IT asset disposition company. Blancco donated the diagnostics and certified data erasure software licenses to ensure every donated smartphone, laptop, and desktop could be safely repurposed for the auction.
In an unprecedented effort for the company, Quick Ship donated 100% of the hammer proceeds from electronics they auctioned through eBay Live – a real-time, interactive livestream shopping experience where buyers can bid on and purchase items as they are showcased.
Quick Ship's inaugural charity auction, held on September 16, benefitted Jonathan's Landing Foundation, a 501c3 nonprofit that builds neuroinclusive housing and workforce pathways for adults with autism, intellectual and development disabilities, and other neurodiversities. To date, the charity has raised $150,000 from the auction, including corporate donations and commitments landed after the show.
"We want to thank Blancco for donating the device diagnostic and data erasure software so that each item crossing the screen is verified, sanitized and buyer-ready," said Jordan Insley, founder and CEO of Quick Ship Brands. "We are also thankful for the credentialing organizations CTIA and WISE; they are a key reason a refurbished device carries real trust behind it. And of course, we couldn't serve worthwhile organizations like Jonathan's Landing at this scale without our industry partners. They generously donated valuable inventory that brings value to buyers and supports good, meaningful work."
"It's an honor to collaborate with Jordan and the entire Quick Ship Brands Team on their eBay Live charity initiative," said Blancco Chief Revenue Officer Tom Salah. "We've been fortunate to partner with QuickShip for many years, and it's incredible to see the impact they continue to make. We are proud to support nonprofits like Jonathan's Landing by helping to ensure every donated device undergoes rigorous processing, including testing and data sanitization. Donors can be confident that sensitive data is completely removed before devices are resold, fostering more donations."
For years, Blancco has donated certified data sanitization software licenses to several charities and charity-supporting organizations, including The Turing Trust and Salvation Army Trading Company, among others, to support reuse across four continents. Blancco's regulation-compliant, secure and certified data erasure processes create necessary assurances for device donors, enabling tens of thousands of personal computing devices to be reused to benefit disadvantaged populations.
For information about future charitable auctions, please visit https://quickshipbrands.com/events. To learn more about Blancco's data sanitization and diagnostics solutions, please visit www.blancco.com.
Reduce Risk. Increase Efficiency. Be Sustainable. Blancco Technology Group provides organizations with secure, compliant, and automated solutions that accelerate the transition to the circular economy. Each year, tens of millions of Blancco erasures allow top-tier organizations to protect end-of-life data against unauthorized access, safely redeploy data storage assets, and firmly comply with increased data protection and privacy requirements. Our precise device diagnostics help move used IT assets confidently into the circular economy, enabling enterprises, IT asset disposition (ITAD) vendors and recyclers, and mobile industry stakeholders to operate more sustainably.
Globally approved, recommended, and certified by governing and industry bodies around the world, Blancco is the industry standard in data erasure and mobile lifecycle solutions. With 40+ patented or patent-pending ideas, we continue to grow the number of innovative solutions global companies can rely on to accelerate operations, secure their data, and grow their businesses. Read more about us at blancco.com.

The company recovers value from consumer trade-ins, K-12 and enterprise device fleets, big-box retail returns, and brand inventory through one engine: devices are tested and authenticated, erased to NIST SP 800-88 with Blancco-certified reporting, graded, valued against live secondary-market data, and sold per unit across eBay, eBay Live, Amazon, Walmart, Best Buy, and its own storefronts. GameStop Still Wants eBay, and Its CEO Is Betting Big on Himself
Ryan Cohen just wrote a personal check for a million shares of his own struggling company, and three directors bought the same week. When a CEO puts tens of millions of his own money in while quarterly sales crater, the…
Published September 23, 2026, 3:47pm ET · 3 min read
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
The prominent GameStop store sign, with its distinctive red and white logo, represents the company's continued presence in the gaming market. This image captures the brand at a crucial time for its financial trajectory. © Dennis Diatel Photography / iStock Editorial via Getty Images
Ryan Cohen wrote a personal check for a million shares of his own company. The filing dated September 10, 2026 shows the purchase at $20.3759 per share, and a director bought the same day. The stock settled the most recent session at $24.04, up 5.62%.
GameStop (NYSE:GME | GME Price Prediction) sales keep sliding while a proposed takeover of eBay (NASDAQ:EBAY), a business several times its size, sits on the risk-factor page of the last 8-K. Open-market purchases with personal money are the most informative signal any insider can send. A chief executive writing a check for tens of millions while quarterly revenue falls almost 19% is likely seeing something the market hasn’t priced in yet.
Three directors bought in the same window: Lawrence Cheng, 55,000 shares at $18.7992 on September 8, James Grube, 10,255 at $19.12 on September 9, and Alain Attal, 5,000 at $20.00 on September 10.
Insider sells have a dozen reasons. Insider buys have one. A purchase at a higher price than the last one carries even more information.
The Q2 FY2027 8-K, filed September 8, 2026, discloses approximately 43.4 million shares of eBay common stock valued at approximately $4.9 billion and continues to reference the proposed acquisition of eBay in forward-looking risk factors.
The word that matters is proposed. The bid has never been formally withdrawn, and the company still flags that it may not be completed.
Revenue in the most recent quarter came in at $790.2 million, down 18.7% year over year, yet operating income jumped to $160.2 million, up 141.27%. Gross margin expanded to 43.7% from 29.1%.
Collectibles hit $356.3 million, up 57%, and now make up 45.1% of net sales. Video games fell to $263.2 million from $494.6 million.
However, I’d ignore the headline net income. It was flattered by a $166.3 million derivative gain tied to eBay and dinged by a $75 million loss on digital assets.
Balance Sheet, Guidance, and the Trigger
Against a market cap of $12.13 billion, GameStop carries $4.85 billion in cash and a $4.9 billion eBay position. A meaningful share of the equity value sits in marketable securities rather than in store operations.
Management raised the fiscal 2026 Adjusted EBITDA outlook to in excess of $650 million from in excess of $600 million. The trigger is a formal withdrawal of the eBay bid, a definitive agreement, or another Cohen buy at a price above $20.3759.
Bull: a chief executive spending real money on his own stock in a coordinated cluster with directors, a collectibles category growing fast enough to reshape the mix, record operating income for the period, and an investment portfolio no other specialty retailer can match.
Bear: total sales are still falling, the crypto position introduces volatility unrelated to the business, and the eBay bid may quietly evaporate into a passive stake that never becomes a deal.
The deciding variable is whether collectibles growth can outrun the legacy business’s decline before the market decides the eBay stake is just an expensive hedge fund position wrapped in a retailer.
