eBay started as a one-person experiment, too. What to value when starting small
Nemoto here!
When we hear stories about large companies, it can feel like they were people from a different world from the very beginning. They had amazing technology, massive amounts of capital, and a clear path to success. We assume that's why they were able to do it.
However, I feel that by looking only at the finished product, we distance ourselves from the actions we can take today. This time, I would like to think about what we should verify in a small business, starting from the origins of eBay.
The entrance to a large market was an individual's trading experiment
The founder of eBay is Pierre Omidyar. In his biography submitted to the SEC, it is explained that he started it as a sole proprietorship in September 1995 and incorporated it in May 1996. You cannot equate the current size of the company with its form at the time of founding.Founder and Management Biography from eBay's 2006 SEC Filing
The initial site was named AuctionWeb. In a letter from the founder in February 1996, he noted that since launching on Labor Day of the previous year, usage had spread beyond his imagination, and he had come to feel that it was a major experiment in testing commercial transactions on the Internet.Pierre Omidyar's Founder Letter dated February 26, 1996
What attracts me to this is the fact that a grand success story wasn't already complete at the start. First, you create a place for transactions. People come there. Interactions occur. By watching those reactions, you gradually see what is needed next.
Of course, just because you know how eBay started doesn't mean that doing the same thing will lead to the same result. The times and the competition are different. However, we can also re-question whether we need to keep increasing our preparations before verifying someone's reaction.
Starting small is different from starting sloppily. Even if you are handling just one product, you still need to confirm its condition, provide a description, determine how to deliver it, and commit to communication. Scaling down is not about letting go of that responsibility, but about creating a scope that you can verify yourself until the end.
Before asking "Did it sell?", what do you want to verify?
For example, suppose someone starting an overseas sales business first researches a single product. If they decide at this point that "if it doesn't sell in a week, I'm not cut out for this," they will overlook what they could have learned. Are they failing to use the words buyers are searching for? Is the condition not being conveyed? Do the price and shipping terms not match? You cannot understand the cause from the result alone.
If it were me, I would first write down just one thing I want to verify with this action. For example, "Can the scratches on this product be conveyed to the other party through photos and descriptions alone?" For that purpose, you can not only increase the number of photos but also have a third party look at them and ask where it is difficult to make a judgment.
The action of generating sales and the action of understanding the state in which you can generate sales are not always the same. If you think about this separately, I think the pain of feeling like your entire self is being evaluated by a single reaction will decrease a little.
I also want to decide the scope of the trial in advance. The time I can use, the amount of money I can put into inventory, the place where I can store items, and the time I can spend answering inquiries. If you expand your experiment to the point of breaking your daily life or commitments, you may find yourself unable to continue before you get any results.
This is not a story about making your dreams small. It is a story about choosing a step that the current you can take responsibility for, in order to continue while protecting the things you love. Precisely because you have resolve, you want to think about a form that allows you to continue.
Turn today's step into a record that allows for the next judgment
What you can do today is make a single memo about the product or service you want to test. "Who do I want to help and with what?" "How is that person doing now?" "Where am I verifying this time?" If you can write these three things in your own words, it becomes easier to determine the priority of your preparations.
After executing, separate what you did from the other party's reaction and keep a record. I changed the description. I retook the photos. There was an inquiry. How many hours did it take to respond? If you keep a record of what actually happened, not just your own impressions, you can choose where to change next.
The less reaction you get, the more you might want to change everything at once. But if you change the product, the price, and the description, you won't know which change was relevant. If it were me, I would fix things one by one, starting from the parts where the reason for review is clear. Of course, problems related to safety or misdescription are handled first.
Before you start, I think it's good to decide when you will look back. The purpose of setting a period is not to decide quickly whether it is a success or a failure. It is to verify what you have learned and what you still do not know using the time you have decided upon. Even if there is no reaction, you can specifically leave behind where to look and the order in which to try things.
Before deciding to "increase products because they aren't selling," you can return to those notes. If you can't keep up with managing the current number, increasing them isn't necessarily the answer. I want to be able to choose the next step based on what I've learned, rather than on a whim.
Another thing I want you to keep track of is what was inconvenient for the customer. Even if you think you've explained it well enough, it might be too long for the other person, or the necessary information might be buried at the end. When you're at a small stage, it should be easier to fix those inconveniences with your own hands.
What I want to cultivate in my business is not just the single event of a sale. It's about the people involved being able to make their own decisions next time, and being able to move forward with more peace of mind than before. I believe that this accumulation is what gives meaning to running a business.
It would be a waste to use the history of eBay only to look at an amazing company. Even for those of us who aren't big yet, we can take action today to reduce one inconvenience. Let's leave that step behind in a way that leads to tomorrow's decisions.

Blancco Donates Diagnostics and Data Erasure Software Licenses for Quick Ship’s eBay Live Charity Auction
All auction proceeds directly benefit Jonathan's Landing, a nonprofit that builds neuroinclusive housing and workforce pathways
Boston, MASSACHUSETTS, Sept. 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Blancco Technology Group, the industry standard in data erasure and mobile lifecycle solutions, today announced its participation in an eBay Live charity auction initiative led by its customer Quick Ship Brands, a certified reverse logistics, refurbishment, and IT asset disposition company. Blancco donated the diagnostics and certified data erasure software licenses to ensure every donated smartphone, laptop, and desktop could be safely repurposed for the auction.
In an unprecedented effort for the company, Quick Ship donated 100% of the hammer proceeds from electronics they auctioned through eBay Live – a real-time, interactive livestream shopping experience where buyers can bid on and purchase items as they are showcased.
Quick Ship's inaugural charity auction, held on September 16, benefitted Jonathan's Landing Foundation, a 501c3 nonprofit that builds neuroinclusive housing and workforce pathways for adults with autism, intellectual and development disabilities, and other neurodiversities. To date, the charity has raised $150,000 from the auction, including corporate donations and commitments landed after the show.
"We want to thank Blancco for donating the device diagnostic and data erasure software so that each item crossing the screen is verified, sanitized and buyer-ready," said Jordan Insley, founder and CEO of Quick Ship Brands. "We are also thankful for the credentialing organizations CTIA and WISE; they are a key reason a refurbished device carries real trust behind it. And of course, we couldn't serve worthwhile organizations like Jonathan's Landing at this scale without our industry partners. They generously donated valuable inventory that brings value to buyers and supports good, meaningful work."
"It's an honor to collaborate with Jordan and the entire Quick Ship Brands Team on their eBay Live charity initiative," said Blancco Chief Revenue Officer Tom Salah. "We've been fortunate to partner with QuickShip for many years, and it's incredible to see the impact they continue to make. We are proud to support nonprofits like Jonathan's Landing by helping to ensure every donated device undergoes rigorous processing, including testing and data sanitization. Donors can be confident that sensitive data is completely removed before devices are resold, fostering more donations."
For years, Blancco has donated certified data sanitization software licenses to several charities and charity-supporting organizations, including The Turing Trust and Salvation Army Trading Company, among others, to support reuse across four continents. Blancco's regulation-compliant, secure and certified data erasure processes create necessary assurances for device donors, enabling tens of thousands of personal computing devices to be reused to benefit disadvantaged populations.
For information about future charitable auctions, please visit https://quickshipbrands.com/events. To learn more about Blancco's data sanitization and diagnostics solutions, please visit www.blancco.com.
Reduce Risk. Increase Efficiency. Be Sustainable. Blancco Technology Group provides organizations with secure, compliant, and automated solutions that accelerate the transition to the circular economy. Each year, tens of millions of Blancco erasures allow top-tier organizations to protect end-of-life data against unauthorized access, safely redeploy data storage assets, and firmly comply with increased data protection and privacy requirements. Our precise device diagnostics help move used IT assets confidently into the circular economy, enabling enterprises, IT asset disposition (ITAD) vendors and recyclers, and mobile industry stakeholders to operate more sustainably.
Globally approved, recommended, and certified by governing and industry bodies around the world, Blancco is the industry standard in data erasure and mobile lifecycle solutions. With 40+ patented or patent-pending ideas, we continue to grow the number of innovative solutions global companies can rely on to accelerate operations, secure their data, and grow their businesses. Read more about us at blancco.com.

The company recovers value from consumer trade-ins, K-12 and enterprise device fleets, big-box retail returns, and brand inventory through one engine: devices are tested and authenticated, erased to NIST SP 800-88 with Blancco-certified reporting, graded, valued against live secondary-market data, and sold per unit across eBay, eBay Live, Amazon, Walmart, Best Buy, and its own storefronts. GameStop Still Wants eBay, and Its CEO Is Betting Big on Himself
Ryan Cohen just wrote a personal check for a million shares of his own struggling company, and three directors bought the same week. When a CEO puts tens of millions of his own money in while quarterly sales crater, the…
Published September 23, 2026, 3:47pm ET · 3 min read
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
The prominent GameStop store sign, with its distinctive red and white logo, represents the company's continued presence in the gaming market. This image captures the brand at a crucial time for its financial trajectory. © Dennis Diatel Photography / iStock Editorial via Getty Images
Ryan Cohen wrote a personal check for a million shares of his own company. The filing dated September 10, 2026 shows the purchase at $20.3759 per share, and a director bought the same day. The stock settled the most recent session at $24.04, up 5.62%.
GameStop (NYSE:GME | GME Price Prediction) sales keep sliding while a proposed takeover of eBay (NASDAQ:EBAY), a business several times its size, sits on the risk-factor page of the last 8-K. Open-market purchases with personal money are the most informative signal any insider can send. A chief executive writing a check for tens of millions while quarterly revenue falls almost 19% is likely seeing something the market hasn’t priced in yet.
Three directors bought in the same window: Lawrence Cheng, 55,000 shares at $18.7992 on September 8, James Grube, 10,255 at $19.12 on September 9, and Alain Attal, 5,000 at $20.00 on September 10.
Insider sells have a dozen reasons. Insider buys have one. A purchase at a higher price than the last one carries even more information.
The Q2 FY2027 8-K, filed September 8, 2026, discloses approximately 43.4 million shares of eBay common stock valued at approximately $4.9 billion and continues to reference the proposed acquisition of eBay in forward-looking risk factors.
The word that matters is proposed. The bid has never been formally withdrawn, and the company still flags that it may not be completed.
Revenue in the most recent quarter came in at $790.2 million, down 18.7% year over year, yet operating income jumped to $160.2 million, up 141.27%. Gross margin expanded to 43.7% from 29.1%.
Collectibles hit $356.3 million, up 57%, and now make up 45.1% of net sales. Video games fell to $263.2 million from $494.6 million.
However, I’d ignore the headline net income. It was flattered by a $166.3 million derivative gain tied to eBay and dinged by a $75 million loss on digital assets.
Balance Sheet, Guidance, and the Trigger
Against a market cap of $12.13 billion, GameStop carries $4.85 billion in cash and a $4.9 billion eBay position. A meaningful share of the equity value sits in marketable securities rather than in store operations.
Management raised the fiscal 2026 Adjusted EBITDA outlook to in excess of $650 million from in excess of $600 million. The trigger is a formal withdrawal of the eBay bid, a definitive agreement, or another Cohen buy at a price above $20.3759.
Bull: a chief executive spending real money on his own stock in a coordinated cluster with directors, a collectibles category growing fast enough to reshape the mix, record operating income for the period, and an investment portfolio no other specialty retailer can match.
Bear: total sales are still falling, the crypto position introduces volatility unrelated to the business, and the eBay bid may quietly evaporate into a passive stake that never becomes a deal.
The deciding variable is whether collectibles growth can outrun the legacy business’s decline before the market decides the eBay stake is just an expensive hedge fund position wrapped in a retailer.

What is the difference between eBay and Sekaimon? What you need to know to avoid losses on your first overseas purchase
As I continue to list items on eBay, I sometimes hear from Japanese buyers who say they use Sekaimon even though they suspect it might actually be cheaper to buy directly on eBay.
As someone who has been on the selling side of eBay for a long time, I have realized through my transactions that the experience of receiving an item can change significantly depending on how you buy it, even for the same product.
In this article, I will organize how eBay and Sekaimon work and what the differences are.
By the time you finish reading, you should have the information you need to decide which one you should choose.
What is the fundamental difference between eBay and Sekaimon?
eBay is an auction and flea market platform where sellers from all over the world list items directly and buyers purchase them directly.
On the other hand, Sekaimon is a service that allows you to view and purchase eBay listings in Japanese, and handles everything from the purchase to international shipping and customs clearance to Japan. service.
In other words, Sekaimon is not eBay itself, but is positioned as an intermediary service that makes eBay products easier to use from Japan.
One reason this difference is hard to understand is that the products displayed on the Sekaimon purchase screen are actually items listed by eBay sellers.
There are many cases where the entry point for buying is different, but the source of the product itself is the same.
Even from my perspective as a seller listing items on eBay, there are actually not many situations where I am conscious of whether a buyer is using Sekaimon or buying directly through eBay.
However, because fees, supported languages, and shipping mechanisms differ significantly, the experience will change depending on which one the buyer chooses.
A typical case is assuming that Sekaimon is an official eBay service.
In reality, it is an independent intermediary service operated by a separate company, and its fee structure and support are also different.
Another is simply comparing the displayed price on Sekaimon to see if it is higher or lower than buying directly on eBay.
Since Sekaimon's fees include international shipping and customs procedures, it is easy to misjudge the actual profit or loss if you compare them without understanding the breakdown of the displayed amount.
I have also had several opportunities to explain this difference in mechanism when buyers asked me about pricing.
In the end, which one is right for you?
Based on what we have covered so far, the answer to the question of whether you should use eBay or Sekaimon comes down to the difference in priority between choosing based solely on low cost versus choosing based on peace of mind and convenience.
Using eBay directly is suitable for those who are comfortable with English correspondence and want to handle everything themselves, including direct communication with sellers and price negotiations.
On the other hand, intermediary services like Sekaimon are suitable for those who are uneasy about communicating in English and would rather prioritize the peace of mind provided by Japanese support and proxy services, even if it means paying some fees.
The key criteria for your decision are how much you can handle in terms of English correspondence, how you compare the total costs including fees, and which support you can rely on in the event of a problem—these three points.
These are not matters of special knowledge, but things anyone can judge if they correctly understand how the systems work.
So, how should you actually compare them and how should you use them differently?
From here on, rather than general principles, you will need actual fee simulations and the specific procedures for how to use them.
Many of the questions regarding "what is the difference between eBay and Sekaimon" can be resolved once you understand the division of roles between the two.
Now that you understand the mechanics, what you need next is to know "how to actually compare them and which one you should choose."
The practical guide for that is explained in this article, complete with specific fee simulations.
If you found this helpful, I would appreciate your support by following, liking, and sharing. Next time, I will cover another practical theme regarding eBay exports.

Should You Buy eBay Stock For Its Cash?
eBay's (EBAY) free cash flow is 5.2% of its market value, against 4.6% for the median S&P 500 company. A stock usually offers more cash for its price than most for one of two reasons. Investors either underrate the business or expect its cash to shrink. A buyer needs to know whether eBay's cash is underrated or about to shrink.
eBay's free cash flow was $2.4 billion over the last twelve months, up from $1.4 billion a year earlier. Free cash flow is the cash left after a company pays its costs and funds its investment.
As a shareholder, you own a share of that cash whether or not eBay pays it out. Every $10,000 of eBay stock comes with about $520 of free cash flow a year. When investors value that cash more highly, the share price tends to follow. The effect is stronger when the cash is growing.
eBay earns revenue on the sales that pass through its marketplace. The revenue comes from fees, advertising and shipping services. In the second quarter of 2026, eBay kept 14% of the value of goods sold as revenue. The marketplace needs little investment. eBay spent $0.6 billion on capital investment out of the $3.0 billion its operations brought in over the last twelve months.
eBay's free cash flow was positive throughout the last three years, but it did not hold steady. Three years ago it was $2.4 billion, the same as today. It fell to $1.5 billion the following year before recovering.
eBay owes little against that cash. Net debt, which is debt minus cash, was $3.8 billion on its latest reported balance sheet. That debt is 8.1% of eBay's market value. eBay's operating profit is 9.9 times its interest bill.
Why Does eBay Stock Yield More Than Most?
eBay stock yields more partly because the price appears to assume its growth is slowing. The stock lost 7.5% over the past three months, while the S&P 500 returned 2.7%.
Management's own forecast shows a slowdown. Adjusted earnings per share grew 17% in the second quarter of 2026. For the third quarter, management guided growth of 1% to 5%.
On its August 5, 2026 call, management explained the slowdown from the second quarter to the third. Most of it comes from harder comparisons with last year, management said. A year ago, eBay had the benefit of the launch of its U.S. Klarna partnership and of triple-digit growth in Pokémon. Both make comparisons in 2026 tougher.
eBay also bought Depop, a resale business, for $1.4 billion in cash on July 30, 2026. Management expected two effects from Depop in the third quarter. Depop would add about 2.5 points to currency-neutral growth in the value of goods sold. The purchase would also take 3 to 4 points off adjusted operating income growth.
eBay's operating margin, its operating profit per dollar of revenue, has already slipped. The margin was 20.5% over the last twelve months, down from 21.3% a year earlier. Even so, management raised its full-year outlook on the August 5 call. Management also expects Depop to add to adjusted operating income in 2028.
Watch eBay's Earnings Growth Against Its Guide
Adjusted earnings growth above the 1% to 5% that management guided would be a sign that eBay's cash is still rising. Growth at the low end, with a lower operating margin, would be a sign of cash levelling off.
eBay's free cash flow is back at its level of three years ago. The risk is that eBay's cash stops rising as its earnings growth slows.
eBay can carry its debt: its operating profit is 9.9 times its interest bill. The open question is growth. The third-quarter 2026 results will show whether eBay keeps growing through harder comparisons and the cost of Depop.
Does This Mean You Should Act On EBAY?
Our purpose is to inform you with unique data so you make the right investment decisions. That said, betting on a single stock is always risky, no matter which direction you choose.
There is a smarter approach. Since its inception, the Trefis High Quality (HQ) Portfolio has returned 105%, beating the benchmark that combines the three major indices - the S&P 500, S&P Mid-cap, and Russell 2000. And it did so without taking the concentrated risk that comes with do-it-yourself stock picking. If that is how you want to invest, the HQ Portfolio is the place to start.

pages.text:
Image Credit: Rahul Pugazhendi / Unsplash.
Buying a replacement airbag from a stranger on the internet always required a certain amount of trust. Considering what happens when one of these safety devices fails, eBay has decided that trust isn't enough anymore.
As of September 24, 2026, eBay no longer permits sellers to list standalone airbags or airbag inflators. Steering wheel airbag covers are included in the prohibition as well.
The marketplace says the decision followed a comprehensive review of the risks these products can pose to users. The change arrives amid heightened scrutiny of dangerous replacement airbag components that have made their way into vehicles in the United States.
Recent findings from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration illustrate just how serious the consequences can be. The agency says one particular type of defective replacement inflator has now been connected to 11 deaths and three severe injuries.
Image Credit: Nebular / Unsplash.
eBay's new policy applies across its airbag category and prohibits any seller from offering airbags or inflators. Sellers were instructed to remove affected active, scheduled, and draft listings by September 24, with eBay saying it would remove remaining listings itself.
There are some exceptions for related components that don't actually contain an airbag or inflator. Outside the United States, items such as airbag control units, crash sensors, diagnostic modules, and passenger sensors can continue to be listed, while U.S. sales of those parts are restricted to currently pre-approved sellers.
Trying to relist prohibited equipment could result in selling restrictions. eBay says listings removed as part of the policy change won't negatively affect a seller's compliance history.
Defective Replacement Inflators Have Killed 11 People
The timing is notable given NHTSA's ongoing warnings about dangerous replacement airbags. In April, the agency took the unusual step of banning the sale and importation of certain frontal driver airbag inflators marked DTN60DB after determining that they contained a safety-related defect.
Instead of operating normally during a collision, the defective inflators can rupture and propel metal fragments into the passenger compartment. NHTSA's latest figures link them to 11 deaths and three severe injuries across 14 crashes in the United States.
The agency says the affected vehicles had previously received replacement driver-side frontal airbag inflators. Known incidents have involved Chevrolet Malibu, Hyundai Sonata, and Chevrolet Equinox models, although NHTSA says it has no information indicating the problem is limited to those vehicles.
This Is One Car Part You Don't Want To Get Wrong
Image Credit: Shutterstock.
Airbags rely on an extremely rapid deployment process to protect occupants during a collision. NHTSA estimates frontal airbags saved more than 50,000 lives over a 30-year period, illustrating just how valuable the technology can be when everything works properly.
The problem is that determining the history and authenticity of a replacement component purchased online isn't always straightforward. NHTSA recommends that owners whose vehicles previously experienced an airbag deployment have replacement equipment inspected by a reputable mechanic, particularly if the repair wasn't performed by the manufacturer's dealership.
Losing easy access to used airbags on eBay might be inconvenient for some repairers and enthusiasts. Still, when the part sitting inches from your face is designed to explosively deploy during a crash, this is one online bargain that's probably better left alone.
If you want more stories like this, follow Guessing Headlights on Yahoo so you don't miss what's coming next.

HP OmniBook 5 combines vibrant OLED visuals, rich audio, and AI-enhanced capabilities to help consumers create, connect and be entertained wherever they go

PALO ALTO, Calif., Oct. 01, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Today, HP Inc. (NYSE: HPQ) announced the new HP OmniBook 5, a premium consumer Windows laptop designed for people who want more from their everyday device: more screen, more battery life, more connectivity and more freedom to create, connect and be entertained without compromise.
“Today's consumers expect technology that fits naturally into their lives – beautifully designed, easy to use, and powerful enough to support everything from collaboration and content creation to entertainment and everyday productivity,” said Samuel Chang, Senior Vice President and Division President, Consumer Personal Systems at HP Inc. “The new HP OmniBook 5 delivers exactly that, bringing together premium design and immersive experiences with a colorful OLED display in an incredibly portable package for work, study, and entertainment.”
Consumers increasingly expect a PC that helps them stay productive, connected, and entertained without adding complexity to their lives. Whether streaming content, attending class, creating, collaborating, or staying connected with friends and family, they want premium experiences that fit their lifestyles, their budgets, and help prepare for what comes next. The HP OmniBook 5 was designed to deliver exactly that: bringing together thoughtful design, immersive entertainment, and everyday practicality in one accessible device.
Designed for students, young professionals and modern multitaskers, the device delivers the experiences people value most, from immersive entertainment to seamless connectivity, in a device built to fit naturally into everyday life:
Empowers productivity and creativity with AI-ready performance: Powered by up to an Intel® Core™ 7 processori with integrated NPU capabilitiesii, the HP OmniBook 5 helps users stay productive, communicate effectively and take advantage of the latest AI-ready experiences across work, school and personal projects.
Adapts to life on the move with up to 42 hours of VPB (Local Video Playback) battery lifeiii and effortless mobility: Combining an ultra-thin 11.77 mm profile, lightweight 1.16 kg design, flexible 180° hinge, dual full-function USB-C®iv ports and HP's compact 65W USB Mini GaN chargerv, the HP OmniBook 5 is built to move effortlessly from campus to café, commute to couch and everywhere in between.
Delivers rich entertainment experiences: Featuring up to a 2.5K OLEDvi touch display, 100% DCI-P3 color coverage, up to 620 nits brightnessvii, HP Eye Ease technology and up to a 90% screen-to-body ratio, the HP OmniBook 5 delivers vivid visuals and immersive entertainment wherever users go.
Enhances seamless collaboration and connection: An FHD IR camera with Windows Hello facial recognition, dual microphones, Poly Studio-tuned audioviii and DTS:X Ultra help users show up clearly and confidently for classes, calls and everyday conversations.
Expresses individuality through thoughtful design: Available in Smoke Silver, Starlit Blue, Peony Pink and Soft Honeydew, the HP OmniBook 5 combines a premium aluminum chassis, tone-on-tone keyboard and refined design details that help consumers choose a device that reflects their personal style.
Premium Design, Built for Growing Businesses
HP is also bringing premium design and AI-ready performance to growing businesses with the HP ProBook 4. Purpose-built for SMBs and mobile professionals, the device delivers the design, mobility and performance growing businesses need without compromising on durability or value.
As HP’s thinnest business notebook,ix the HP ProBook 4 pairs a sleek 12mm thinx aluminum design with real portability, starting at just 2.6 lbs.,xi so it travels light without feeling delicate. The device comes in three finishes – Eclipse Gray, Atmospheric Blue, and Mist Silver – with a 14-inch 2.8K OLED displayxii bringing work to life with rich 100% DCI-P3 color and fluid 120Hz motion.
Powered by up to an Intel® Core™ 7 processori with up to 17 TOPS NPU AI accelerationxiii, up to 32 GB of memory and up to 1TB of storage, the HP ProBook 4keeps everyday productivity and AI-enhanced work moving. A 70Whr battery with HP Fast Charge,xiv along with MIL-STD durability,xv helps professionals work confidently.
The HP OmniBook 5 14 AI PC is expected to be available on HP.com and Best Buy in October for a starting price of $699.99.
The HP ProBook 4 G2iS 14 AI PC is expected to be available on HP.com in November. Pricing will be announced closer to availability.

HP Inc. has officially expanded its consumer lineup with the introduction of the new HP OmniBook 5, designed to bring premium Windows AI PC experiences to a wider audience. Announced on October 1, 2026, the flagship addition—anchored by the HP OmniBook 5 14 AI PC—delivers larger screens, exceptional battery longevity, and versatile connectivity without the steep price tag typically associated with flagship notebooks.
“Consumers increasingly expect a PC that helps them stay productive, connected, and entertained without adding complexity to their lives,” said the HP product team in the official launch announcement. “The HP OmniBook 5 makes premium design and intelligent features accessible to more buyers than ever before.”
HP OmniBook 5 Delivers “Groundbreaking” Battery and Performance
The headline engineering achievement of the HP OmniBook 5 is its staggering battery endurance. According to HP’s official specifications, the laptop supports up to an incredible 42 hours of local video playback on a single charge, obliterating traditional multi-day workflows and making charger anxiety a thing of the past.
When users finally do need to top up, fast-charging technology allows the machine to jump from empty to a 50 percent charge in just 30 minutes. That combination of marathon runtime and rapid refueling redefines what consumers can expect from a mainstream portable.
Immersive Display and Modern Connectivity
Built for streaming, content creation, and daily productivity, the HP OmniBook 5 pairs its energy-efficient processor architecture with a vibrant, color-accurate display and slim bezels. Wireless connectivity is fully modernized with Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.3 support, while physical I/O includes an HDMI 2.1 output port, two versatile USB Type-C jacks, and a headphone and microphone combo port.
This feature set ensures seamless pairing with external monitors, docks, and high-res audio gear, mirroring the robust connectivity trends we have analyzed in previous Techaeris mobile hardware coverage.
Expanding the Ecosystem With ProBook 4 G2iS
Alongside the consumer reveal, HP also pulled back the curtain on the new HP ProBook 4 G2iS 14 AI PC. Tailored for small businesses and hybrid professionals, the ProBook 4 G2iS brings enterprise-grade security, durable chassis engineering, and AI-accelerated productivity tools into a streamlined commercial package designed to keep mobile workforces secure and efficient.
Together, the HP OmniBook 5 and the ProBook 4 showcase HP’s strategy to democratize artificial intelligence across both consumer and enterprise tiers, giving everyday users tools previously reserved for high-end workstations.

The companion HP ProBook 4 G2iS will also roll out through HP’s enterprise channels. International buyers should check regional HP storefronts for localized pricing in CAD, EUR, or GBP.

HP’s MacBook Neo Competitor Might Cost You More Than You Think
A colorful shell and pretty screen set the HP OmniBook 5 apart. But make sure to pay attention to the RAM spec.
HP's cheapo laptop is the only one that comes with a colorful, pretty OLED screen. © HP
Apple’s MacBook Neo really kicked all the other laptop makers in the pants earlier this year, and now even HP is trying its hand at a low-cost laptop that doesn’t feel “cheap.” The cheerfully colorful OmniBook 5 packs in a few features no other Neo clone has, but I would still be wary about its price point if I were you.
From the jump, HP wants you to know the OmniBook 5 starts at just $700, the same opening cost of the Apple MacBook Neo. However, that price only accounts for 8GB of LPDDR5-6400 MT/s RAM. If you look on HP’s store page, that’s the only config currently available. Based on my tests with similar laptops, 8GB is not enough to allow for a clean Windows 11 experience. Microsoft is in the process of fixing that, but you shouldn’t buy anything now that provides just the bare hope Windows 11 won’t suck as much in the future.
HP has another configuration with 16GB of RAM, and it says it will launch a version with 12GB sometime in November. A spokesperson for HP told Gizmodo that the 16GB version “is planned” but that the company doesn’t have pricing or availability details to share at this time.
The HP OmniBook 5 comes in Smoke Silver, Starlit Blue, Peony Pink, and Soft Honeydew. © HP
At the very least, the laptop seems light at 2.56 pounds. The MacBook Neo weighs in at 2.7 pounds. The base model also comes with a bare 256GB of storage—same as the MacBook Neo—though you’ll supposedly be able to stretch that to 1TB. The $700 OmniBook 5 model also comes with an Intel Core 5 320 chip, an example from Intel’s Wildcat Lake lineup that has been seen in many low-cost PCs these last few months. You can push the performance with up to an Intel Core 7 350, though that version won’t be around until October.
Let’s take a minute to look at the full arena of MacBook Neo competitors. Dell has two operating at that sub-$1,000 price point, the Dell XPS 13 and Dell 14S. Acer is spinning up a Swift Air 14 with a similar suite of pastel shells. Those laptops are sticking with Intel, but Lenovo is the odd man out with its upcoming IdeaPad Vibe laptops. Those clamshells go even further with vibrant colorways and processor options between an AMD Ryzen AI 400 series chip or a Qualcomm Snapdragon X CPU.
HP is sticking with the same vein of these other brands, simultaneously offering something none of the competition has: an OLED display. Every version of this laptop comes with some variety of organic light-emitting diode screens, which offer a much better sense of contrast than a typical LCD screen. The laptop will launch with options for a touch and non-touch version at 2K resolution (1,920 x 1,200). A 2.5K (2,560 x 1,600) will be along sometime in March 2027. Just know that each screen may not be the brightest of its kind, with a typical luminance of around 300 nits, according to HP’s specs page.
There’s a lot to like here, but I can’t help but feel downtrodden. MacBooks can get away with 8GB of unified memory because—well—macOS is simply better designed for lower memory configurations than Windows 11. Just last month, Dell hiked the costs of its XPS 13, and now the 16GB model costs $1,000. Apple too spiked the price of its MacBook models a few months ago, and I don’t imagine the gouging will falter as we head to the end of 2026. I hope HP can maintain prices on its new OmniBook. Call me a pessimist, but I’m not holding my breath.

HP is announcing a new laptop that’s squarely aimed at Apple’s MacBook Neo. The 2026 HP OmniBook 5 14 starts at $699.99 with an Intel Core 5 315 “Wildcat Lake” processor, 8GB of RAM, and a 256GB SSD. Much of that sounds pretty familiar, being in lockstep with both Apple’s Neo and its recent competition from Dell, Asus, and Acer — the HP even offers a similar four color options in silver, pink, blue, and green. But one thing that separates the OmniBook is its inclusion of an OLED display on all configs.
The OmniBook 5 14 can be configured much higher, with up to a Core 7 350 chip, 16GB of RAM, and a 1TB SSD, but all models include a 1080p webcam, dual speakers, HDMI, 3.5mm audio jack, and just two 10Gbps USB-C ports. A touchscreen version will be available when the OmniBook 5 launches in October, but a version with a 2560 x 1600 resolution OLED and 400 nits of brightness isn’t coming until March 2027.
While the OmniBook 5 14 doesn’t seem poised to best the MacBook Neo in raw processing power (based on our other reviews of Wildcat Lake laptops) or screen brightness, it’s quite thin, light, and colorful. HP even gave it the nicer, sleeker lid logo usually reserved for pricier models. It starts at just 2.56 pounds, and it’s as thin as 0.46 inches / 11.7mm. That’s slightly lighter and thinner than a Neo. And I’d expect its Wildcat Lake chips to offer some good-to-great battery life. But we’ll have to see how it delivers in actual testing.

Why Is HP (HPQ) Up 5.1% Since Last Earnings Report?
It has been about a month since the last earnings report for HP (HPQ). Shares have added about 5.1% in that time frame, outperforming the S&P 500.
Will the recent positive trend continue leading up to its next earnings release, or is HP due for a pullback? Before we dive into how investors and analysts have reacted as of late, let's take a quick look at its latest earnings report in order to get a better handle on the important drivers.
HPQ's Q3 Earnings Surpass Expectations, Revenues Rise Y/Y
HP reported third-quarter fiscal 2026 adjusted earnings of 83 cents per share, which increased 10.7% year over year and beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 10.7%.
HPQ reported revenues of $15.68 billion, which increased 12.5% and surpassed the consensus mark by 5.6%. Growth was led by Personal Systems as pricing and a richer premium mix offset lower unit volumes.
HPQ's total PC units fell 16% year over year, while AI PCs accounted for 46% of shipment mix, highlighting the shift toward higher-value configurations.
HPQ's Personal Systems Revenues Hit a Q3 Record
Personal Systems revenues were $11.77 billion, up 18.5% year over year and 16.7% in constant currency. Commercial PS revenues rose 22%, while Consumer PS revenues increased 10%, reflecting continued strength across both customer groups.
Commercial PC units declined 14%, and consumer units fell 19%. Even so, HP gained 2.6 points of share in premium categories and 1.8 points in workstations sequentially. Attached businesses, including peripherals, collaboration solutions and services, contributed about one-third of Personal Systems gross profit.
HPQ Printing Revenues Slip on Lower Volumes
Printing revenues were $3.91 billion, down 2.2% year over year and 3.6% in constant currency. Supplies revenues declined 3%, Commercial Printing fell 1%, and Consumer Printing decreased 2% as hardware and supplies volumes remained under pressure.
The company continued to shift toward higher-value print categories. Tank printer units jumped 42%, while Industrial Printing posted its 12th consecutive quarter of revenue growth. 3D Printing revenues also grew at a double-digit rate for the sixth straight quarter.
HPQ's gross margin was 18.8%, pressured by higher commodity costs and a greater mix of Personal Systems revenues. Non-GAAP operating margin contracted 60 basis points year over year to 6.5%, even as pricing, growth in key areas and tariff refunds provided partial offsets.
Personal Systems operating margin fell 80 basis points to 4.6%, while Printing margin improved 110 basis points to 18.1%. The quarter's adjusted earnings included an 11-cent benefit from tariff refunds. Management said the benefit from lower-cost inventory is largely behind the company as higher-cost inventory moves through results.
HPQ's Cash Flow Supports Capital Returns
HPQ generated $1.74 billion of operating cash flow and $1.57 billion of free cash flow in the quarter. The company ended July with $4.17 billion in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash, while the cash conversion cycle stood at negative 37 days.
During the quarter, HPQ repurchased $300 million of stock and paid $274 million in dividends. It also paid down slightly more than $500 million of debt maturities, ending the quarter with $9.20 billion of gross debt.
HPQ expects AI PCs to account for 50% of shipment mix by the end of fiscal 2026, rising to 60-70% in fiscal 2027 and more than 70% in fiscal 2028. The company is also working with more than 150 software partners to expand workloads that can run locally on PCs.
Beyond PCs, HPQ signed a three-year, $100 million strategic agreement with RRD to accelerate AI and industrial automation in print production. Management also highlighted continued expansion of WXP, which brings PC, printer and collaboration-device management into a single platform.
HPQ Raises Fiscal 2026 Earnings and Cash Flow Outlook
HPQ raised its fiscal 2026 non-GAAP earnings outlook to $3.19-$3.29 per share from $2.90-$3.10. The new range includes a 19-cent favorable impact from estimated tariff refunds. Free cash flow guidance was also increased to $3-$3.20 billion.
For the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, HPQ expects non-GAAP earnings of 69-79 cents per share, including an 8-cent tariff-refund benefit. Personal Systems revenues are expected to be below seasonal levels but still grow year over year, while Printing revenues are projected to follow historical seasonality.
How Have Estimates Been Moving Since Then?
In the past month, investors have witnessed a upward trend in estimates revision.
The consensus estimate has shifted 12.36% due to these changes.
Currently, HP has a subpar Growth Score of D, however its Momentum Score is doing a lot better with an A. Following the exact same course, the stock was allocated a grade of A on the value side, putting it in the top 20% for value investors.
Overall, the stock has an aggregate VGM Score of A. If you aren't focused on one strategy, this score is the one you should be interested in.
Estimates have been trending upward for the stock, and the magnitude of these revisions looks promising. It comes with little surprise HP has a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). We expect an above average return from the stock in the next few months.

HP Brings Premium PC Experiences to More Consumers
News Highlights:
HP OmniBook 5 combines vibrant OLED visuals, rich audio, and AI-enhanced capabilities to help consumers create, connect and be entertained wherever they go
HP ProBook 4 equips growing businesses with AI-ready performance and portability to stay productive wherever work happens
PALO ALTO, Calif., Oct. 01, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Today, HP Inc. (NYSE: HPQ) announced the new HP OmniBook 5, a premium consumer Windows laptop designed for people who want more from their everyday device: more screen, more battery life, more connectivity and more freedom to create, connect and be entertained without compromise.
“Today's consumers expect technology that fits naturally into their lives – beautifully designed, easy to use, and powerful enough to support everything from collaboration and content creation to entertainment and everyday productivity,” said Samuel Chang, Senior Vice President and Division President, Consumer Personal Systems at HP Inc. “The new HP OmniBook 5 delivers exactly that, bringing together premium design and immersive experiences with a colorful OLED display in an incredibly portable package for work, study, and entertainment.”
Consumers increasingly expect a PC that helps them stay productive, connected, and entertained without adding complexity to their lives. Whether streaming content, attending class, creating, collaborating, or staying connected with friends and family, they want premium experiences that fit their lifestyles, their budgets, and help prepare for what comes next. The HP OmniBook 5 was designed to deliver exactly that: bringing together thoughtful design, immersive entertainment, and everyday practicality in one accessible device.
Designed for students, young professionals and modern multitaskers, the device delivers the experiences people value most, from immersive entertainment to seamless connectivity, in a device built to fit naturally into everyday life:
Empowers productivity and creativity with AI-ready performance: Powered by up to an Intel® Core™ 7 processori with integrated NPU capabilitiesii, the HP OmniBook 5 helps users stay productive, communicate effectively and take advantage of the latest AI-ready experiences across work, school and personal projects.
Adapts to life on the move with up to 42 hours of VPB (Local Video Playback) battery lifeiii and effortless mobility: Combining an ultra-thin 11.77 mm profile, lightweight 1.16 kg design, flexible 180° hinge, dual full-function USB-C®iv ports and HP's compact 65W USB Mini GaN chargerv, the HP OmniBook 5 is built to move effortlessly from campus to café, commute to couch and everywhere in between.
Delivers rich entertainment experiences: Featuring up to a 2.5K OLEDvi touch display, 100% DCI-P3 color coverage, up to 620 nits brightnessvii, HP Eye Ease technology and up to a 90% screen-to-body ratio, the HP OmniBook 5 delivers vivid visuals and immersive entertainment wherever users go.
Enhances seamless collaboration and connection: An FHD IR camera with Windows Hello facial recognition, dual microphones, Poly Studio-tuned audioviii and DTS:X Ultra help users show up clearly and confidently for classes, calls and everyday conversations.
Expresses individuality through thoughtful design: Available in Smoke Silver, Starlit Blue, Peony Pink and Soft Honeydew, the HP OmniBook 5 combines a premium aluminum chassis, tone-on-tone keyboard and refined design details that help consumers choose a device that reflects their personal style.
Premium Design, Built for Growing Businesses
HP is also bringing premium design and AI-ready performance to growing businesses with the HP ProBook 4. Purpose-built for SMBs and mobile professionals, the device delivers the design, mobility and performance growing businesses need without compromising on durability or value.
As HP’s thinnest business notebook,ix the HP ProBook 4 pairs a sleek 12mm thinx aluminum design with real portability, starting at just 2.6 lbs.,xi so it travels light without feeling delicate. The device comes in three finishes – Eclipse Gray, Atmospheric Blue, and Mist Silver – with a 14-inch 2.8K OLED displayxii bringing work to life with rich 100% DCI-P3 color and fluid 120Hz motion.
Powered by up to an Intel® Core™ 7 processori with up to 17 TOPS NPU AI accelerationxiii, up to 32 GB of memory and up to 1TB of storage, the HP ProBook 4keeps everyday productivity and AI-enhanced work moving. A 70Whr battery with HP Fast Charge,xiv along with MIL-STD durability,xv helps professionals work confidently.
The HP OmniBook 5 14 AI PC is expected to be available on HP.com and Best Buy in October for a starting price of $699.99.
The HP ProBook 4 G2iS 14 AI PC is expected to be available on HP.com in November. Pricing will be announced closer to availability.

The HP OmniBook 5 Brings MacBook Neo Competitor to Market at $699.99
HP introduces the HP OmniBook 5 14 AI PC starting at $699.99, offering up to 42 hours of battery life, immersive displays, and broad availability.
MeWeXMastodonRedditThreadsBlueskyWhatsAppFacebookGrokLinkedInShare
HP Inc. has officially expanded its consumer lineup with the introduction of the new HP OmniBook 5, designed to bring premium Windows AI PC experiences to a wider audience. Announced on October 1, 2026, the flagship addition—anchored by the HP OmniBook 5 14 AI PC—delivers larger screens, exceptional battery longevity, and versatile connectivity without the steep price tag typically associated with flagship notebooks.
“Consumers increasingly expect a PC that helps them stay productive, connected, and entertained without adding complexity to their lives,” said the HP product team in the official launch announcement. “The HP OmniBook 5 makes premium design and intelligent features accessible to more buyers than ever before.”
HP OmniBook 5 Delivers “Groundbreaking” Battery and Performance
The headline engineering achievement of the HP OmniBook 5 is its staggering battery endurance. According to HP’s official specifications, the laptop supports up to an incredible 42 hours of local video playback on a single charge, obliterating traditional multi-day workflows and making charger anxiety a thing of the past.
When users finally do need to top up, fast-charging technology allows the machine to jump from empty to a 50 percent charge in just 30 minutes. That combination of marathon runtime and rapid refueling redefines what consumers can expect from a mainstream portable.
Immersive Display and Modern Connectivity
Built for streaming, content creation, and daily productivity, the HP OmniBook 5 pairs its energy-efficient processor architecture with a vibrant, color-accurate display and slim bezels. Wireless connectivity is fully modernized with Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.3 support, while physical I/O includes an HDMI 2.1 output port, two versatile USB Type-C jacks, and a headphone and microphone combo port.
This feature set ensures seamless pairing with external monitors, docks, and high-res audio gear, mirroring the robust connectivity trends we have analyzed in previous Techaeris mobile hardware coverage.
Expanding the Ecosystem With ProBook 4 G2iS
Alongside the consumer reveal, HP also pulled back the curtain on the new HP ProBook 4 G2iS 14 AI PC. Tailored for small businesses and hybrid professionals, the ProBook 4 G2iS brings enterprise-grade security, durable chassis engineering, and AI-accelerated productivity tools into a streamlined commercial package designed to keep mobile workforces secure and efficient.
Together, the HP OmniBook 5 and the ProBook 4 showcase HP’s strategy to democratize artificial intelligence across both consumer and enterprise tiers, giving everyday users tools previously reserved for high-end workstations.

Battery Life: Up to 42 hours of local video playback on a single charge

The HP OmniBook 5 14 AI PC carries a starting price of $699.99 USD and is scheduled to be available for order in October 2026 through HP and Best Buy. Affordable laptops often make you choose between a nice screen and a machine you’d want to carry. HP’s $699.99 OmniBook 5 14 makes a different pitch against Apple’s MacBook Neo: an OLED touchscreen wrapped in a slim, colorful aluminum body. It’s an appealing combination for someone moving between classes, work, and a movie, though the price doesn’t buy every specification HP advertises for the series.
HP treats color as part of the laptop, rather than something to add with a sticker. Starlit Blue, Peony Pink, Soft Honeydew, and Smoke Silver give the aluminum chassis some character, with a tone-on-tone keyboard to keep the look together. At 2.6 pounds and 0.46 inches thick, it could slip into a bag without looking like an anonymous office machine when it comes back out.
Open the lid and the 14-inch OLED touchscreen becomes the reason to look twice. Its 16:10 proportions leave more vertical room for a document or editing tools, while touch makes a quick tap feel natural. But the $699.99 model has a 1920×1200 resolution and a 300-nit brightness rating, not the up-to-2.5K, 620-nit display mentioned in HP’s broader launch announcement.
The 180-degree hinge is a smaller detail, but it might be the one you appreciate when sharing a draft across a cafe table. Lay the laptop flat, turn it toward a friend, and neither of you has to hunch over the keyboard. The backlit keys make a difference when that conversation stretches into the evening, although this isn’t a tablet you can fold backward.
HP also makes room for an HDMI 2.1 port, two USB-C connections, and a headphone jack. If you need to show a presentation on a meeting room display or connect a monitor at work, you might not need to hunt for an adapter. The catch is that there’s no USB-A port listed, so an older mouse or flash drive could still send you looking.
Underneath the colorful shell, this configuration has an Intel Core 5 320 processor, 8GB of onboard memory, and a 256GB SSD. Those numbers should keep expectations in check if you juggle large creative files and a dozen browser tabs. There’s a 512GB storage option, but it shouldn’t be confused with what the starting price includes.
Battery life deserves careful reading. HP touts up to 42 hours for the series, but that figure comes from local video playback, not a day of calls, spreadsheets, and multitasking. The listed 60Wh battery and a claimed 50% charge in about 30 minutes are useful details when you’re planning a day out. Neither tells you when you’ll need an outlet.
The HP OmniBook 5’s challenge to the MacBook Neo isn’t about winning every specification. It offers a different set of priorities: a touchscreen, OLED contrast, cheerful colors, and ports that could save you from carrying an adapter. The modest memory and storage are harder to overlook. Still, it’s good to see an affordable laptop make its strongest argument the moment you open it.

HP’s MacBook Neo Competitor Might Cost You More Than You Think
A colorful shell and pretty screen set the HP OmniBook 5 apart. But make sure to pay attention to the RAM spec.
HP's cheapo laptop is the only one that comes with a colorful, pretty OLED screen. © HP
Apple’s MacBook Neo really kicked all the other laptop makers in the pants earlier this year, and now even HP is trying its hand at a low-cost laptop that doesn’t feel “cheap.” The cheerfully colorful OmniBook 5 packs in a few features no other Neo clone has, but I would still be wary about its price point if I were you.
From the jump, HP wants you to know the OmniBook 5 starts at just $700, the same opening cost of the Apple MacBook Neo. However, that price only accounts for 8GB of LPDDR5-6400 MT/s RAM. If you look on HP’s store page, that’s the only config currently available. Based on my tests with similar laptops, 8GB is not enough to allow for a clean Windows 11 experience. Microsoft is in the process of fixing that, but you shouldn’t buy anything now that provides just the bare hope Windows 11 won’t suck as much in the future.
HP has another configuration with 16GB of RAM, and it says it will launch a version with 12GB sometime in November. A spokesperson for HP told Gizmodo that the 16GB version “is planned” but that the company doesn’t have pricing or availability details to share at this time.
The HP OmniBook 5 comes in Smoke Silver, Starlit Blue, Peony Pink, and Soft Honeydew. © HP
At the very least, the laptop seems light at 2.56 pounds. The MacBook Neo weighs in at 2.7 pounds. The base model also comes with a bare 256GB of storage—same as the MacBook Neo—though you’ll supposedly be able to stretch that to 1TB. The $700 OmniBook 5 model also comes with an Intel Core 5 320 chip, an example from Intel’s Wildcat Lake lineup that has been seen in many low-cost PCs these last few months. You can push the performance with up to an Intel Core 7 350, though that version won’t be around until October.
Let’s take a minute to look at the full arena of MacBook Neo competitors. Dell has two operating at that sub-$1,000 price point, the Dell XPS 13 and Dell 14S. Acer is spinning up a Swift Air 14 with a similar suite of pastel shells. Those laptops are sticking with Intel, but Lenovo is the odd man out with its upcoming IdeaPad Vibe laptops. Those clamshells go even further with vibrant colorways and processor options between an AMD Ryzen AI 400 series chip or a Qualcomm Snapdragon X CPU.
HP is sticking with the same vein of these other brands, simultaneously offering something none of the competition has: an OLED display. Every version of this laptop comes with some variety of organic light-emitting diode screens, which offer a much better sense of contrast than a typical LCD screen. The laptop will launch with options for a touch and non-touch version at 2K resolution (1,920 x 1,200). A 2.5K (2,560 x 1,600) will be along sometime in March 2027. Just know that each screen may not be the brightest of its kind, with a typical luminance of around 300 nits, according to HP’s specs page.
There’s a lot to like here, but I can’t help but feel downtrodden. MacBooks can get away with 8GB of unified memory because—well—macOS is simply better designed for lower memory configurations than Windows 11. Just last month, Dell hiked the costs of its XPS 13, and now the 16GB model costs $1,000. Apple too spiked the price of its MacBook models a few months ago, and I don’t imagine the gouging will falter as we head to the end of 2026. I hope HP can maintain prices on its new OmniBook. Call me a pessimist, but I’m not holding my breath.

Getting the conversation ready...
HP’s answer to the MacBook Neo is thinner, lighter, and comes with OLED
﻿The HP OmniBook 5 14 looks like a Neo wannabe right down to its 8GB of RAM and colors, but it seems a compelling competitor.
﻿The HP OmniBook 5 14 looks like a Neo wannabe right down to its 8GB of RAM and colors, but it seems a compelling competitor.
Does this range of colors look a little familiar? Image: HP
The Neo Effect: How Apple’s cheapest Mac is changing the PC game
is a reviewer covering laptops and the occasional gadget. He spent over 15 years in the photography industry before joining The Verge as a deals writer in 2021.
HP is announcing a new laptop that’s squarely aimed at Apple’s MacBook Neo. The 2026 HP OmniBook 5 14 starts at $699.99 with an Intel Core 5 315 “Wildcat Lake” processor, 8GB of RAM, and a 256GB SSD. Much of that sounds pretty familiar, being in lockstep with both Apple’s Neo and its recent competition from Dell, Asus, and Acer — the HP even offers a similar four color options in silver, pink, blue, and green. But one thing that separates the OmniBook is its inclusion of an OLED display on all configs.
The OmniBook 5 14 can be configured much higher, with up to a Core 7 350 chip, 16GB of RAM, and a 1TB SSD, but all models include a 1080p webcam, dual speakers, HDMI, 3.5mm audio jack, and just two 10Gbps USB-C ports. And while the inclusion of OLED across the range is a major draw to the new OmniBook, the base config only has a passable 1920 x 1200 resolution and 300 nits of max brightness on its non-touch panel. A touchscreen version will be available when the OmniBook 5 launches in October, but a version with a 2560 x 1600 resolution OLED and 400 nits of brightness isn’t coming until March 2027.
While the OmniBook 5 14 doesn’t seem poised to best the MacBook Neo in raw processing power (based on our other reviews of Wildcat Lake laptops) or screen brightness, it’s quite thin, light, and colorful. HP even gave it the nicer, sleeker lid logo usually reserved for pricier models. It starts at just 2.56 pounds, and it’s as thin as 0.46 inches / 11.7mm. That’s slightly lighter and thinner than a Neo. And I’d expect its Wildcat Lake chips to offer some good-to-great battery life. But we’ll have to see how it delivers in actual testing.
Alongside the OmniBook 5 14, HP is also announcing a new ProBook 4 G2iS business laptop that it claims at 0.47 inches / 12mm is its “thinnest business notebook.” It’ll also start with Intel Wildcat Lake chips, 8GB of RAM, and a 256GB SSD when it launches in December, but there’s no price yet.

Why Is HP (HPQ) Up 5.1% Since Last Earnings Report?
It has been about a month since the last earnings report for HP (HPQ). Shares have added about 5.1% in that time frame, outperforming the S&P 500.
Will the recent positive trend continue leading up to its next earnings release, or is HP due for a pullback? Before we dive into how investors and analysts have reacted as of late, let's take a quick look at its latest earnings report in order to get a better handle on the important drivers.
HPQ's Q3 Earnings Surpass Expectations, Revenues Rise Y/Y
HP reported third-quarter fiscal 2026 adjusted earnings of 83 cents per share, which increased 10.7% year over year and beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 10.7%.
HPQ reported revenues of $15.68 billion, which increased 12.5% and surpassed the consensus mark by 5.6%. Growth was led by Personal Systems as pricing and a richer premium mix offset lower unit volumes.
HPQ's total PC units fell 16% year over year, while AI PCs accounted for 46% of shipment mix, highlighting the shift toward higher-value configurations.
HPQ's Personal Systems Revenues Hit a Q3 Record
Personal Systems revenues were $11.77 billion, up 18.5% year over year and 16.7% in constant currency. Commercial PS revenues rose 22%, while Consumer PS revenues increased 10%, reflecting continued strength across both customer groups.
Commercial PC units declined 14%, and consumer units fell 19%. Even so, HP gained 2.6 points of share in premium categories and 1.8 points in workstations sequentially. Attached businesses, including peripherals, collaboration solutions and services, contributed about one-third of Personal Systems gross profit.
HPQ Printing Revenues Slip on Lower Volumes
Printing revenues were $3.91 billion, down 2.2% year over year and 3.6% in constant currency. Supplies revenues declined 3%, Commercial Printing fell 1%, and Consumer Printing decreased 2% as hardware and supplies volumes remained under pressure.
The company continued to shift toward higher-value print categories. Tank printer units jumped 42%, while Industrial Printing posted its 12th consecutive quarter of revenue growth. 3D Printing revenues also grew at a double-digit rate for the sixth straight quarter.
HPQ's gross margin was 18.8%, pressured by higher commodity costs and a greater mix of Personal Systems revenues. Non-GAAP operating margin contracted 60 basis points year over year to 6.5%, even as pricing, growth in key areas and tariff refunds provided partial offsets.
Personal Systems operating margin fell 80 basis points to 4.6%, while Printing margin improved 110 basis points to 18.1%. The quarter's adjusted earnings included an 11-cent benefit from tariff refunds. Management said the benefit from lower-cost inventory is largely behind the company as higher-cost inventory moves through results.
HPQ's Cash Flow Supports Capital Returns
HPQ generated $1.74 billion of operating cash flow and $1.57 billion of free cash flow in the quarter. The company ended July with $4.17 billion in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash, while the cash conversion cycle stood at negative 37 days.
During the quarter, HPQ repurchased $300 million of stock and paid $274 million in dividends. It also paid down slightly more than $500 million of debt maturities, ending the quarter with $9.20 billion of gross debt.
HPQ expects AI PCs to account for 50% of shipment mix by the end of fiscal 2026, rising to 60-70% in fiscal 2027 and more than 70% in fiscal 2028. The company is also working with more than 150 software partners to expand workloads that can run locally on PCs.
Beyond PCs, HPQ signed a three-year, $100 million strategic agreement with RRD to accelerate AI and industrial automation in print production. Management also highlighted continued expansion of WXP, which brings PC, printer and collaboration-device management into a single platform.
HPQ Raises Fiscal 2026 Earnings and Cash Flow Outlook
HPQ raised its fiscal 2026 non-GAAP earnings outlook to $3.19-$3.29 per share from $2.90-$3.10. The new range includes a 19-cent favorable impact from estimated tariff refunds. Free cash flow guidance was also increased to $3-$3.20 billion.
For the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, HPQ expects non-GAAP earnings of 69-79 cents per share, including an 8-cent tariff-refund benefit. Personal Systems revenues are expected to be below seasonal levels but still grow year over year, while Printing revenues are projected to follow historical seasonality.
How Have Estimates Been Moving Since Then?
In the past month, investors have witnessed a upward trend in estimates revision.
The consensus estimate has shifted 12.36% due to these changes.
Currently, HP has a subpar Growth Score of D, however its Momentum Score is doing a lot better with an A. Following the exact same course, the stock was allocated a grade of A on the value side, putting it in the top 20% for value investors.
Overall, the stock has an aggregate VGM Score of A. If you aren't focused on one strategy, this score is the one you should be interested in.
Estimates have been trending upward for the stock, and the magnitude of these revisions looks promising. It comes with little surprise HP has a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). We expect an above average return from the stock in the next few months.

FSLR Stock Heads For Its Worst Week In Over A Month — Roth Says US Polysilicon Crackdown Could Provide A Tailwind
Roth said First Solar’s recent selloff comes amid tighter U.S. import rules, but expects reduced stockpiling to support polysilicon and module pricing.
Workers are inspecting among large areas of photovoltaic solar panels in the Gobi wasteland.(Photo credit should read CFOTO/Future Publishing via Getty Images)
Roth called current FSLR levels a “very attractive entry point” despite concerns over weaker-than-expected solar-module pricing.
The firm also sees T1 Energy and Toyo as potential beneficiaries.
New U.S. rules target polysilicon stockpiling, with Roth saying more than 20 importer licenses have already been revoked.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
First Solar (FSLR) was on investors’ radar on Friday after Roth Capital said a crackdown on polysilicon stockpiling could tighten supplies and support higher pricing for domestic solar manufacturers.
The call comes after FSLR shares tumbled nearly 11% on Thursday and headed for their biggest weekly loss in six weeks. Roth attributed the selloff to concerns that solar-module pricing may not be as strong as previously expected.
However, the brokerage sees the recent weakness as a buying opportunity, calling current levels a “very attractive entry point.”
Advertisement|Remove ads.
At the time of writing, FSLR stock was up 3.5%
Roth Says FLSR Could Benefit From Supply Tailwinds
Earlier this week, the Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security implemented a temporary rule to prevent companies from stockpiling polysilicon and related products before new Section 232 import measures take effect on December 4. The rule allows the government to restrict companies that import significantly more polysilicon than their historical levels, while new importers are subject to weekly limits.
The move follows President Donald Trump’s August proclamation imposing minimum import prices on polysilicon, wafers, solar cells, and modules, as well as a 15% tariff on covered polysilicon derivatives beginning in December.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
Roth said its channel checks showed imports had increased more than expected and that it learned more than 20 importer licenses had already been revoked. The firm expects stricter enforcement to reduce stockpiling, restrict supply and ultimately support higher U.S. pricing.
The firm sees First Solar, T1 Energy (TE) and Toyo (TOYO) as potential beneficiaries.
First Solar reported a mixed second quarter. While revenue fell 4% to $1.06 billion, partly due to customer contract terminations, earnings rose 23% to $3.92 per share.

The company also maintained its full-year outlook, forecasting $4.9 billion to $5.2 billion in sales and adjusted earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) of $2.6 billion to $2.8 billion. The company ended June with a contracted backlog of 45.1 GW extending through 2030.

By Trader EdgeSeptember 24, 2026No Comments3 Mins Read
FSLR shares plummeted approximately 8% and hit a 52-week bottom at $182.88
Year-to-date losses have reached nearly 27% in 2026
Robert W. Baird’s revised price target triggered the latest decline

Shares of First Solar tumbled approximately 8% during Wednesday’s trading session, hitting a 52-week bottom at $182.88. The sharp decline wiped away additional gains the solar manufacturer had accumulated during what initially appeared to be a promising year.
Year-to-date performance now shows losses approaching 27% since January 2026 began. This represents a dramatic turnaround from the elevated levels witnessed during the stock’s earlier peak.
The company’s 52-week peak stands at $320.95. Wednesday’s trading bottom demonstrates the substantial distance the shares have traveled downward from that previous zenith.
The selloff materialized following Robert W. Baird’s decision to reduce its price forecast for First Solar. This updated assessment amplified investor concerns regarding the company’s financial trajectory entering 2026.
Baird’s adjustment arrives amid indications of reduced clarity surrounding upcoming order bookings. Market participants are simultaneously monitoring escalating ambiguity concerning U.S. renewable energy regulations and utility-scale project appetite.
Contracted Orders Extend Through Decade’s End
First Solar maintains a substantial pipeline of committed contracts extending through 2030. This extensive order book provides the organization with an extended timeline of anticipated revenue generation despite near-term demand fluctuations.
The contracted pipeline enables more predictable production scheduling and assists in stabilizing earnings throughout market turbulence. Nevertheless, quarterly revenue figures have demonstrated inconsistency lately.
Regulatory uncertainties surrounding import duties and trade enforcement actions may perpetuate demand instability for the foreseeable future. Certain overseas manufacturing facilities might experience continued underutilization consequently.
Such underutilization presents potential margin compression risks moving forward. Management has not communicated specific expectations regarding when capacity utilization rates might recover.
Wall Street Remains Divided on Stock Outlook
First Solar hasn’t lost support from all corners of Wall Street. BMO Capital Markets elevated the stock to Outperform status with a $263 price objective earlier in the current year.
BMO analysts argued the preceding selloff appeared excessive considering the established tariff structure and minimum import pricing framework currently implemented. Mizuho Securities similarly maintained its Outperform stance, increasing its target to $324.
Mizuho highlighted revised average selling prices as a potential catalyst for earnings growth. Notably, Baird itself had previously elevated First Solar to Outperform prior to Wednesday’s reduction, emphasizing opportunities within utility-scale installations.
The stock currently commands a price-to-earnings multiple of 11.93. Its PEG ratio registers at 0.31, which certain investors interpret as undervalued considering expansion prospects.
Daily trading volume for First Solar averages approximately 2.14 million shares. The company’s current market capitalization stands around $21.58 billion.
Technical indicators presently suggest a Buy signal for the equity. This assessment persists despite Wednesday’s descent to a fresh yearly low.

Patent complaint withdrawal weighs on the share price
A key short-term catalyst for First Solar Inc. stock is the company’s recent decision to withdraw a patent infringement complaint related to its TOPCon intellectual property before the U.S. International Trade Commission, a move that coincided with a visible price reaction. According to Ground News on September 20, 2026, First Solar voluntarily withdrew the complaint, seeking termination of the ITC investigation without prejudice and framing the step as procedural rather than a retreat from its patent claims.
The company’s general counsel Jason Dymbort indicated that the withdrawal reflects a recalibration of how First Solar enforces its TOPCon-related patents in light of recent U.S. trade measures on polysilicon imports that address some of the border concerns previously targeted through the ITC case, according to Ground News. The market nevertheless reacted negatively in the very short term: First Solar stock fell about 5 percent on the day of the withdrawal, touching its lowest level in roughly five months and underscoring investor sensitivity to any perceived change in the company’s intellectual-property enforcement strategy, Ground News reports.
Analysts see upside despite recent volatility
Against this backdrop, the broader analyst community continues to view First Solar Inc. stock constructively, even if ratings are not uniformly bullish. According to MarketBeat on September 20, 2026, First Solar carries a consensus rating of Moderate Buy based on 1 strong buy, 22 buy, 12 hold and 2 sell recommendations, with an average price target of USD 266.06. With the shares around USD 195.96, this target implies upside potential of about 35.8 percent from the current level, signaling that most covering analysts expect the stock to recover further over time.
A separate view compiled by MarketBeat on September 20, 2026, reiterates that First Solar’s average target of USD 266.06 sits well above the USD 195.96 level at which the stock opened the most recent completed session, leaving the shares trading roughly a quarter below estimated fair value in that assessment. For investors, this gap between price and consensus target is one of the central axes of the current investment case: if First Solar executes on its project pipeline and maintains its cost advantages, the analyst community sees room for the stock to move higher.
Beyond analyst targets, First Solar occupies a leading position among listed renewable energy companies by market capitalization, which adds context to the stock’s current valuation. A sector overview from StockMarketRanks dated September 20, 2026, shows First Solar at the top of a renewable energy ranking, with a market capitalization of about USD 21.06 billion and a share price of USD 195.96, placing it first on that list by market cap. The same overview notes that the stock declined 2.59 percent in the latest trading session, underlining that the recent patent-related headline and broader sector volatility have translated into short-term pressure on the share price.
At the current valuation, First Solar trades at a price-to-earnings ratio of roughly 12.08 based on recent earnings data, according to MarketBeat. The combination of a double-digit billion market capitalization and a low-teens earnings multiple positions First Solar as a large-cap renewable energy name that investors currently pay a relatively modest multiple for, at least compared with some other growth-oriented clean-energy peers. That valuation, together with the approximately 28 percent discount to certain analyst targets mentioned in a trading overview by Pluang on September 20, 2026, is central to how many investors weigh risk and reward.
The recalibration of First Solar’s TOPCon intellectual-property enforcement described by Ground News highlights one of the key risks investors currently monitor: how effectively the company can defend its patents while navigating shifting trade policies. The fact that the stock dropped about 5 percent and touched a five-month low on the day the ITC complaint was withdrawn suggests that market participants worry about potential weakening of IP leverage, even though the company insists the change is procedural and leaves open the option of refiling later.
Another risk is execution against the growth and profitability expectations embedded in consensus targets. As MarketBeat data show, analysts collectively see roughly 35.8 percent upside to the USD 266.06 average target from the USD 195.96 share price. If module demand, project timelines or policy support were to weaken, that upside scenario could be challenged and the current valuation discount might reflect not just short-term sentiment but deeper concerns. For now, however, the predominance of buy ratings over sells indicates that most covering analysts still regard First Solar as fundamentally well positioned within the global solar supply chain.
